t: Install A9 Snap, take your first screenshot, and find your way around the tray icon and the Home window. A9 Snap is a free screenshot tool for Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit). You press a key, then click a window, press F for the whole screen, or drag a box around part of it. The picture is on your clipboard, ready to paste, and saved as a numbered PNG file. There is no account to make and nothing to sign in to.

Install The easiest way to get A9 Snap is the Microsoft Store. It installs with no Windows warning, and Windows keeps it up to date for you. Click the badge above. A9 Snap's page in the Microsoft Store opens in a new tab. Click Get (or Install ). Windows installs A9 Snap for you. Open A9 Snap once after installing , from the Store page or the Start menu. The Store doesn't start it for you, and that first launch is when A9 Snap switches on Start at login . It opens the Home window so you can see it is running. If A9 Snap does not open, find A9 Snap in the Start menu. Already installed A9 Snap from a9snap.com? Keep using it. The Store version is a separate install with its own settings. If you can't or would rather not use the Microsoft Store, Install A9 Snap shows the other way.

Take your first screenshot Press Alt + Z from any app. The screen freezes and dims, and a crosshair follows your pointer. Click a window to capture it (it is outlined as you point), press F for the whole screen, or click and drag a box around what you want. A small readout shows its size, such as 640 × 220. Let go. The picture is now on your clipboard and saved in your screenshots folder. A small note at the bottom right says Copied and gives the file name. Switch to a chat, an email or a document and press Ctrl + V . To change your mind, press Esc before you let go. Take a screenshot covers windows, the whole screen, the crosshair, the magnifier and several monitors. To copy the words rather than a picture, press Alt + X instead and select the text: local OCR puts plain text on the clipboard and saves no file. This is a Pro feature.

The tray icon A9 Snap waits in the tray, the row of small icons next to the clock. Its icon is the Bullseye. If you do not see it, click the ^ arrow by the clock to show hidden icons. Closing the A9 Snap window does not quit it, so the hotkeys keep working. Double-click the icon to open the Home window. Right-click the icon for the menu: Capture region , OCR capture , Recent captures , Open screenshots folder , Manual , Settings , Check for updates and Quit . A single left click shows the same menu a moment later. A small warning badge on the icon means another app has taken one of your hotkeys. See If something goes wrong . To quit A9 Snap, right-click the icon and choose Quit .

The Home window The Home window, with mock captures. Home is where you start. On the left are the Capture and Recent captures buttons, each showing its hotkey, then Editor and Folder , and a menu of settings sections. In the middle are your six newest captures. Click one to draw on it. The Home window explains every part. The Manual row under the menu opens this manual in your browser.

From the Microsoft Store This is the way we recommend. Windows installs A9 Snap for you and keeps it up to date. Click the badge, then click Get (or Install ) on the Store page. Open A9 Snap once after it installs. Getting started shows what you see.

Download the installer If you can't or would rather not use the Microsoft Store, install A9 Snap with the installer from this page. Download the installer The button saves the newest A9Snap-Setup-x64.exe . Then: Open the file. If Windows shows Windows protected your PC , click More info , then Run anyway . Follow the installer. It installs for your Windows user only and does not ask for administrator rights. A9 Snap starts by itself when the installer finishes. The first time, it opens the Home window so you can see it is running. Windows shows that warning because early builds are not signed with a Windows certificate yet. Windows warns about any program it has not seen many times. It is not a finding about A9 Snap. There is no account, and A9 Snap sends nothing beyond its update check (and Pro's license check, if you buy Pro). See Privacy . The installer version checks for updates by itself. You can pick the update channel in Updates and about . See Updates and channels .

Which one should I pick? It is the same app either way, so pick the one that suits you. The Microsoft Store version updates through the Store and skips the Windows warning. The installer version updates itself and lets you pick the update channel. Already installed A9 Snap from a9snap.com? Keep using it. The Store version is a separate install with its own settings.

Click a window, press F for the screen or drag a box; Esc cancels. The picture is saved like any capture: numbered file, clipboard, confirmation, strip and your settings. Only the free ways to capture are offered, even with Pro, and no Pro message appears. A picture of an app on your Always secure list is kept secure and not handed to the other app. One at a time. 0.19.0 · November 26, 2026 Ready to send, in A9 View (free). The result's size in pixels and on disk shows next to the original's as you choose (a very large WebP shows an "about" size at once and the exact one a moment later). Everything happens on your PC and the original is never changed. Where it goes. Save beside the original as name (ready).jpg (then (ready 2) ), Save as new capture (a capture is always a PNG), or Copy . A folder that can't be written to says so and offers Save as new capture. The colour profile is kept, because without it colours would change. See-through areas become white in a JPG, with a note; an animated picture gives its first frame, with a note; a type A9 Snap can't write (such as GIF or HEIC) becomes a PNG with a note. Batch (Pro). Save side by side writes both as the next numbered capture with a small gap and labels ( Before and After , editable), ready to go through Ready to send like any picture. Pro. 0.16.1 · November 25, 2026 Fixed: Trim made a diagonal smear of most recordings. A video whose width is not a multiple of 16 (nearly every recording of a region you drag, for example 780 wide) came out of Trim with the right length and sound but a picture sheared into diagonal streaks, because each decoded row was read as exactly as wide as the picture while the decoder pads its rows. Trim now reads the row width and layout the decoder reports for every frame, for any width and height. The original was never touched; trim the recording again from the original. The same fix for a video's thumbnail and Save as GIF. They read frames the same way, so the strip's thumbnail for such a video and a GIF made from it were sheared too; both are right now. Save this frame was never affected (the player draws that picture). A frame layout A9 Snap can't read stops the job with a plain message ("A9 Snap can't read how this video's picture is stored, so nothing was made.") and writes no file: it never saves a video it can't vouch for. Tests. A new end-to-end script, scripts/e2e/trim-picture.mjs , trims videos at 780 x 1080, 1278 x 718, 642 x 362 and 1280 x 720 (made by ffmpeg and recorded by A9 Snap) and compares the pictures with the original's by SSIM, along with Save this frame and the strip's thumbnail; the 0.16.0 tests only checked length and sound, and used 1280 wide, where the decoder's rows are as wide as the picture.

h: Capture a window, a screen or a region
t: Capture a window, a screen or a region Press Alt + Z and the screen freezes. What you do next decides what you get: Click a window. As you move the pointer, the window under it gets a Volt outline, with its title and its size. Click, and the picture is that window, the way you see it on the frozen screen, without the invisible border Windows puts around it. The picture is cut from the frozen screen, so it shows what you see: if another window overlaps it, the overlap is in the picture too. Click the bare desktop, or press F . You get the whole monitor the pointer is on. Over the desktop the whole monitor is outlined and labelled Screen , so you can see what a click will take. Drag a box. You get exactly the region you drag. The window outline goes away as soon as you start to drag. A hint at the bottom of the monitor you are on lists these keys: Click a window · Drag a region · F full screen · S secure · R record (Pro) · L scroll (Pro) · Esc cancel . It stays for the first few seconds of every capture, and on screen the whole time for your first five captures. Press S before you let go to make it a secure capture (Pro): it stays out of the strip, Windows' clipboard history and your screenshots folder. Press R to record the area as a video instead, with sound if you switch it on (Pro): see Record video and GIF . Press L to scroll the area and join it into one tall picture (Pro): see Scrolling capture . The hint has no S, R or L when you press Alt + X , because an OCR capture saves no picture. A window that stretches over two monitors is cut to the monitor you click on. A maximized window is captured without the taskbar. Pressing Alt + X uses the same picker, so you can click a window to copy its text.

Capture a region Press Alt + Z . Every monitor freezes and dims. A crosshair, a small bullseye and a magnifier follow your pointer. Move to one corner of what you want. Press the mouse button and drag to the opposite corner. The box stays bright. Four Volt corner marks frame it, and a readout shows its size, such as 640 × 220. A tiny drag, under 4 pixels, is a click, and takes the window or screen instead. Let go. The picture is on your clipboard and saved as the next numbered file in your screenshots folder. Dragging a region. The pointer is at the bottom right corner, and the magnifier shows the pixels under it. A note appears at the bottom right of the monitor you captured, for example Copied · SNAP-0042.png . It goes away by itself after a moment. If you turn the confirmation off in General , problems still show.

Without Pro, Alt + X , the Copy text item in the Home window and the tray item open the Pro sheet instead of the picker, and nothing is read or copied. Press Alt + X . The same picker opens. Drag around the text you want and let go. The recognized words go on your clipboard as plain text. Paste them with Ctrl + V . Tip: press and hold at the first corner, look at the magnifier, and nudge the pointer until the corner is exactly where you want it. Then drag.

The file is saved as the next number in your screenshots folder. See Where screenshots go . The note is a button. Every capture is saved to your screenshots folder as a PNG, as well as going to the clipboard. This page covers the folder, the file names and the clipboard option. File names and numbering New files are named SNAP-0042.png : a prefix, a number and .png . The first picture in an empty folder is SNAP-0001.png . A9 Snap reads the folder on every capture. The new number is the highest one it finds, plus one. It never fills gaps and never overwrites a file. If you delete SNAP-0007.png , the next capture is still the highest number plus one. When you delete the newest capture from A9 Snap (the trash can or Delete ), its number also stays taken, even after A9 Snap restarts (the number is kept in the hidden .a9snap folder), so the next capture doesn't reuse it and Next file never goes backwards. A file you delete in Explorer is not remembered: the folder decides. It counts only files named like your prefix, with the number after it and .png , .mp4 or .gif at the end: a recording and a GIF made from it take the next number like a picture, so SNAP-0042.png is followed by SNAP-0043.mp4 . It ignores letter case, and treats - , _ , a space or nothing between the prefix and the number as the same. With the prefix SNAP- , it counts SNAP-0042.png , snap_7094.png and Snap 12.png . It does not count IMG_0042.png or notes.png . Until you change Prefix or Digits , and the folder already has such a sequence, the next file copies the style of the highest-numbered one: the same letter case, the same separator and the same number of digits. A folder whose newest file is SNAG-7094.png gets SNAG-7095.png next, whatever the prefix in Settings says. The File name row has two boxes. Prefix is the text before the number (the default is SNAP- ). Digits is how many digits the number has, padded with zeros, from 0 to 6, and 0 means no padding. A number that needs more digits is written in full: SNAP-1000.png with Digits 3. Change Prefix or Digits and new captures use them from the next one on. The number still comes from the folder, so SNAP-019.png in the folder and Digits set to 4 gives SNAP-0020.png : the count never restarts and a number is never used twice. Files you already have are never renamed. Until you change one of them, A9 Snap keeps following the files already in the folder, and a line under File name says so when that gives a different name than the boxes show. Next file under it is always the real name, read from your folder as you change things. Secure captures follow the same rule inside their own folder. A prefix can't be empty and can't contain \ / : * ? " < > | .

Also copy as file Most apps paste a picture straight from the clipboard. A few want an attachment instead, such as some chat and email apps. Turn on Also copy as file and the saved file goes on the clipboard too, next to the picture. Apps take whichever they understand. It is off by default.

When something can't be saved If the folder is not writable or the disk is full, you still get the picture on your clipboard. The note says Copied · not saved and gives the reason, and it stays for five seconds even if you turned confirmations off. Pick a different folder in Saving .

Search inside screenshots (Pro) You remember what was in the picture: an error message, an order number, a name. With Pro, type those words in the strip's search box and the strip finds the capture. How: press Ctrl + F or / and type. The search matches the file name, the app, the window title and the text inside the picture , ignoring capital letters. order 4417 finds a capture that shows "Order 4417" anywhere on it. How A9 Snap reads them: right after each capture is saved, a background worker reads its text with the same on-device Windows text recognition that Alt+X and Copy text use. It runs at low priority and never delays a capture or the strip. Captures from before Pro was on are read gradually, newest first, a few every minute (faster when you have left the PC alone), until the folder is covered. A capture you edit is read again after you save it. A capture you delete leaves the index, and Undo reads it again. Settings: Search inside screenshots in Saving is on by default with Pro. A line under it says how far the reading is, Read 412 of 1,280 captures , then All captures read . Clear text index deletes everything read so far (it asks first; reading starts again, newest first, unless the setting is off). Turning the setting off stops reading and deletes the index. Languages: the words are read in the languages Windows has text recognition for on your PC. If a language is missing, add it in Windows Settings under Time & language. Without Pro: the search matches only the file name, app and window title, and nothing is read.

Where the words are kept In .a9snap\text.json , in the hidden folder inside your screenshots folder, next to the edit originals and captures.json . The index holds text from your screenshots , so treat it like them: it stays on this PC, is never sent anywhere and is never written to the log. Delete .a9snap before you share the whole folder, or press Clear text index . Secure captures are never read or indexed : they are not in your screenshots folder and the reading never looks in the secure folder. See Privacy .

Scroll to the rest The strip keeps its rows the same height and scrolls . With a search or a chip on, every match is reachable: use the mouse wheel, the arrow keys past the last row, or PageUp and PageDown . The line under the chips says 48 captures when you can scroll to all of them, and Showing 12 of 48 when the strip is only showing your newest. Thumbnails load as the captures scroll into view.

Edit a capture Press H to share the picked captures (Pro). Press E to open the picked capture in the editor . If you picked none or several, E opens the one with the focus ring. Double-clicking a capture does the same. A small Volt dot next to a name means the capture has been edited and its original is kept.

Recordings and GIFs A recording ( .mp4 ) or a GIF made from one is in the strip like a picture, in the same numbering. Its card shows the first frame, a play badge and its length. Enter or a double-click plays it in A9 View (or, with Open my recordings in A9 View off in Settings, your default player); Ctrl + C copies the file, and dragging it out, Delete and Undo work as for a picture. Search finds it by its name and by the app and window title noted when it started. E and the editor do not open recordings, and Copy text and Copy redacted work on pictures only. See Record video and GIF .

The right-click menu Right-click a capture for: Edit opens it in the editor. (A recording's menu has Open , Share… , Save as GIF for a recording up to 30 seconds, Show in folder , Copy path and Delete ; a GIF's has the same without Save as GIF .) Share… (Pro) opens the Windows Share sheet on the capture, or on the whole selection when the capture is part of one. H does the same for the picked captures or the focused one. See Share to your apps . Copy text recognizes the text in the picture with Windows' built-in OCR and puts it on the clipboard as plain text. It changes no file. A9 Snap says Text copied , or No text found if there was nothing to read. Open opens the file in your default picture app. Show in folder opens Explorer with the file selected. Copy path puts the file's full path on the clipboard. Delete moves the file to the Recycle Bin. If the capture is part of a larger selection, the whole selection goes.

Delete a screenshot Three ways, all the same: Point at a capture and click the small red trash can that appears in its top-right corner. Pick one or more captures and press Delete . With nothing picked, Delete removes the capture with the focus ring. Choose Delete in the right-click menu. The captures go to the Recycle Bin, not away for good, and so does the hidden original the editor kept for an edited one. The strip stays open and fills the space with the next capture. A note says Deleted SNAP-0042.png , or Deleted 3 screenshots , with an Undo button for 6 seconds. Undo puts the files back under the same names, exactly as they were. After that you can still restore them from the Recycle Bin. A deleted capture keeps its number while A9 Snap is running, so the next capture is never given the number of the one you just threw away. If Windows can't move a file, because another app has it open, the capture stays and the note says why.

Drag captures out Drag one capture, or the whole selection, out of the strip. They go as files, so you can drop them into Explorer, a browser chat box, Teams or Outlook. If the capture you drag is part of a larger selection, the whole selection goes.
Close the strip Press Esc (twice if the search box has text in it), click anywhere outside it, or press the hotkey again. Closing never touches your clipboard.

h: How many captures it shows, and how many to a row
t: How many captures it shows, and how many to a row The strip shows 12 captures by default, and the search reaches the rest. Captures in the strip in Strip and editor can be 6, 9, 12, 18 or 24, and Per row can be 4, 6, 8 or 12. The default is 12 captures, 6 to a row: two rows of six. The strip is centred on the monitor your pointer is on and never wider than its work area: if a row doesn't fit, it holds fewer, and if the rows don't fit the height, you scroll. The strip lists only files named like your prefix, such as SNAP-0042.png . See Where screenshots go .

Open a capture in the editor and add an arrow, a box, some text, numbered steps, a stamp, a highlight, a blur or a crop, then send it. The editor is deliberately small. It has nine tools and nothing more, so marking up a screenshot takes a few seconds. Everything you draw stays editable until you save. The editor on a mock capture: a box, an arrow and a text label, with the toolbar above.

h: Open a capture in the editor
t: Open a capture in the editor Pick whichever is closest: In the strip , select a capture and press E , double-click it, or right-click it and choose Edit . Click Edit on the note that appears after a capture. On the Home window, click one of the six captures, or click Editor to open the newest capture. Turn on Open the editor after every capture in Strip and editor to open it automatically. In A9 View , press E on any picture: the same tools come up in that window, and a picture that is not a capture is never changed (saving writes a copy next to it). There the Ellipse is O , because E leaves.

Draw something Choose a tool from the toolbar, or press its key. Drag on the picture. A line under the picture tells you what the tool does. Pick a colour and a width in the toolbar. They apply to what you draw next. Keep going, then press Ctrl + S or click Done to save. See Saving, Save as new and Revert . The colours are Nine Red, Volt, Ink, White and Blue. The widths are Thin, Medium and Thick. The highlighter starts out Volt.

The tools Tool Key What it does Select V Click a shape to select it, drag to move it, drag its handles to resize it. Change its colour or width, or press Delete to remove it. Arrow A Drag from the tail to where the head should be. The head is where you let go. Box B Drag out a rectangle outline. Ellipse E Drag out an oval outline. Highlight H Drag over what matters. It paints a translucent band, Volt by default. Text T Click, type, then press Enter to finish. Shift + Enter starts a new line. Esc cancels. The width sets the text size. Steps N Each click drops the next numbered circle (1, 2, 3 …) in the current colour and width. Drag while you place one to pull a pointer tail out of it. Stamps M Pick a stamp (check, cross, question, exclamation or star) from the row that appears, then click to place it. Drag instead of clicking to size it as you place it. Blur U Drag over what to hide. It turns the area into flat blocks. Crop C Drag the region to keep, adjust it with the handles, then press Enter . Esc cancels. To fix a text, double-click it. Text uses Geist with a soft dark outline, so it reads on any background.

Steps Steps are for showing someone how to do something. Click where step 1 goes, then step 2, and so on: the numbers count the steps in the order you placed them. The width sets the circle's size, and the number is black or white, whichever reads on the colour. Drag while you press to add a pointer tail that points at what the step is about. Select a step to move it, change its colour or width, or drag the end of its tail; drag the tail back onto the circle to remove it. Delete a step and the rest renumber (the step after 2 becomes 2), and undo and redo bring the old numbers back.

Stamps The stamps are drawn by A9 Snap in its own colours, not emoji, so they look the same everywhere: a check (Volt), a cross (Nine Red), a question (Blue), an exclamation (White) and a star (Volt). Pick one from the row that appears while the tool is on, then click to place it at a medium size. Select a stamp to move it, drag a corner handle to resize it (it stays square), change its colour, or, with the Select tool, click another stamp in the row to swap it.

Drop shadow The Shadow button in the top bar adds a soft shadow and a 40-pixel see-through margin around the picture you save, and around the copy on the clipboard. It is part of the document, so undo brings it back out, and with a crop the shadow goes around the cropped picture. The margin makes the saved file larger than the capture; the footer says so while it is on. Programs that can read a transparent PNG (chat apps, Word, browsers) show the shadow over their own background; a program that can only take a plain bitmap gets the picture on white. Turn on Drop shadow in the editor in Strip and editor to have every picture open with the shadow on. It is off by default.

Blur Blur pixelates for real. The saved file holds flat blocks where the area was, not the picture with a layer on top, so nobody can lift the blur off later. Before you save, undo still brings the pixels back. After you save, see the note on originals .
Crop Drag a region, then press Enter to apply it. The footer shows the new size and the original size. Undo brings the whole picture back until you save.

Backgrounds With A9 Snap Pro , click Background in the toolbar to put the picture on a backdrop: room around it, a colour or a gradient behind it, rounded corners and a shadow. It is how a screenshot stops looking like a raw screenshot when you paste it into a chat, a document or a post. It works the same in the editor window and in A9 View . A mock capture on a gradient backdrop, with the Background settings open. Clicking Background puts the picture on the style you used last, or the standard one the first time (64 pixels of room, the Ocean gradient, 12-pixel corners, a soft shadow). A row of settings opens under the toolbar, and the picture on screen changes as you move them: Padding: 0 to 200 pixels around the picture. Backdrop: None (see-through), a solid colour, one of eight gradients, or your own two-colour gradient with the two colour boxes at the end of the row. Corners: 0 to 40 pixels of rounding on the picture. Shadow: Off, Soft or Strong. Shape: Auto (the same room on every side), 16:9, 4:3 or 1:1. The picture stays in the middle and the backdrop grows to fit the shape. Click Background again to take it off. Undo and redo work on it like on any other change, and dragging a slider is one undo step. Share-ready is the same thing in one click: it puts the picture on the background you used last, without any settings in the way. Whatever you set is remembered between sessions, on this PC only. The order is crop first, then the background, so the backdrop always wraps the picture you are keeping. While the Crop tool is on, the background steps aside so you can see what you are cutting. The marks you drew (arrows, text, blur) stay on the picture, inside the backdrop.

What gets saved The background is part of the picture you save, so it is in the file, in the copy on the clipboard, and in whatever you share or drag out after saving. The footer shows the size the file will have, for example saved as 608 × 428 with a background . A capture keeps its untouched original like after any edit: Revert brings back the plain picture, or open it again and change or remove the background. A picture that is not a capture follows the A9 View rules : a copy named (edited) next to it, or Save as new capture . A backdrop of None with rounded corners or a shadow leaves see-through parts. A PNG keeps them. A JPG or BMP cannot, so when you save one the editor says so in a line under the toolbar, and the see-through parts are filled with white. A very large picture can be too big for a background (a side of more than 16,000 pixels). The editor says so and leaves the picture as it was. While a background is on, the plain Shadow button is off, because the background has its own shadow. In A9 View the small map for a zoomed picture is hidden while a background is on. Backgrounds are a Pro feature. Without Pro, Background and Share-ready carry a PRO badge, and clicking either opens the Pro sheet and changes nothing. There are no keyboard shortcuts for them and no setting to turn on: the last style is remembered by itself.

Redact With A9 Snap Pro , press R or click Redact in the top bar to blur every email address, phone number and card number in the picture in one go, with your own patterns and words . Each one becomes an ordinary Blur you can move, delete or undo, and the Hidden list at the top right says what found each. See Auto-redact .

Share Click Share in the top bar (Pro) to send the picture to an app. A9 Snap saves what is on screen over the capture, as Done does, closes the editor and opens the Windows Share sheet on the saved file. Without Pro the button carries a PRO badge and opens the Pro sheet; nothing is saved. See Share to your apps .

Copy text Click Copy text in the top bar to recognize the picture currently on screen with Windows' built-in OCR and put the words on the clipboard as plain text. This includes an unsaved crop or annotation, so what you see is what gets recognized. The editor stays open, your document keeps its unsaved state, and no file is written. A9 Snap says Text copied , or No text found when there was nothing to read.

Undo, redo and zoom Ctrl + Z undoes. Ctrl + Y or Ctrl + Shift + Z redoes. They go back through the whole session, not just the last shape. Ctrl +scroll zooms around the pointer. Ctrl + 0 shows the picture at 100%. The zoom button in the top bar switches between fit and 100%. Scroll to move around a zoomed picture. You can also hold Space and drag, or drag with the middle button.

p: Saving, Save as new and Revert
h: Saving, Save as new and Revert
t: Save over the capture, save as a new numbered file, or go back to the original. Here is exactly what each one does to your files. When you finish drawing, you have two ways to save and one way back. This page explains each, and what happens to the untouched original.

p: Saving, Save as new and Revert
t: Save over the capture Press Ctrl + S or click Done . A9 Snap keeps the untouched original first, if it has not already (see Where originals are kept ). It writes your edit over the same file, under the same name. The numbering never changes. It puts the result on the clipboard, as the picture and as the file, just like a capture. A note says Saved · SNAP-0042.png · copied , and the editor closes. If you did not change anything, Done just closes the editor and writes nothing.

p: Saving, Save as new and Revert
t: Save as new Press Ctrl + Shift + S or click Save as new . The edit is saved as the next numbered file, the highest number plus one, in the folder's own style. The original capture is left exactly as it was. The result goes on the clipboard and the note says Saved as · SNAP-0043.png · copied . Use this when you want to keep both the plain screenshot and the marked-up one.

p: Saving, Save as new and Revert
t: Close without saving Press Esc . If you have changes that are not saved, the editor asks inside its own window: Save your changes? with three buttons. The question the editor asks when you close with unsaved changes. Save saves over the capture, like Done . Enter chooses it. Discard closes and keeps the file as it was. Cancel goes back to editing. Esc chooses it. Esc works from the inside out: it first leaves a text you are typing, then a drag, then a crop waiting for Enter , and only then asks about closing.

p: Saving, Save as new and Revert
t: Revert Revert puts the original picture back. It shows in the top bar only when the capture has an original to go back to, which means you have saved an edit over it at least once. Open the edited capture in the editor . Click Revert . Read Go back to the original? It says the file is replaced by the picture as it was captured and that your edits to it are lost. Click Revert to confirm, or Cancel . A note says Reverted · SNAP-0042.png . The original is removed from its hidden folder once it is back, so a second Revert has nothing to go back to until you save another edit.

p: Saving, Save as new and Revert
t: Where originals are kept The first time you save an edit over a capture, A9 Snap copies the untouched picture into a hidden folder named .a9snap inside your screenshots folder. The copy is named like SNAP-0042.orig.png . A second edit keeps the first original, never an earlier edit. The numbering ignores that folder, so editing changes no number. The strip and the Home window show an edited capture with a small Volt dot. Deleting a capture with the trash can or Delete sends its hidden original to the Recycle Bin with it, and Undo brings both back. Deleting the file in Explorer leaves the original behind. Save as new creates a file with no original of its own, because the plain capture is still there. A capture saved by Redact every capture before it's copied is kept the same way: the file is the blurred picture and its original is the untouched one, so Revert brings the original back. See Auto-redact .

p: Saving, Save as new and Revert
h: Blur is permanent in the saved file
t: Blur is permanent in the saved file A blur turns the area into flat blocks in the file you save. The pixels it hid are gone from that file. But the original, which is the picture before any edit, still holds them, and it stays in .a9snap until you Revert or delete it. To get rid of the originals without touching anything else, press Clear on the Edit originals row in Saving . It moves them to the Recycle Bin and Revert is no longer available for those captures; the edited pictures keep their Volt dot. Before you share a whole screenshots folder, delete the .a9snap folder inside it. Sharing a single file is safe, because the original is not inside that file.

The one window A9 Snap has: your actions on the left, your newest captures in the middle, a Quick capture page, and every setting a click away. Open the Home window by double-clicking the tray icon, or by choosing Settings in the tray menu. It always opens on Home, however you left it. Closing the window does not quit A9 Snap: it keeps waiting in the tray. The tray menu also has Suggest a feature , which opens the feedback page in your browser. The Home window on mock captures.

The left side Capture starts a screenshot, just like the hotkey. Your capture hotkey shows on the button. Secure capture is there only when Pro is on, under Capture . It opens the picker with secure capture already on, and shows Alt+Z, S . Editor opens your newest capture in the editor . It is dimmed until you have a capture. Folder opens your screenshots folder in Explorer. Secure (Pro only, beside Editor and Folder) opens the secure folder in Explorer. With Encrypt the secure folder on, the button reads Vault and opens the vault: Windows asks for Windows Hello first. The menu has three rows, and a row only ever changes what the window shows: Home , Quick capture and Settings . Nothing in the menu takes a picture. The row you are on has a Volt bar. Use the up and down arrow keys to walk them. Quick capture opens its own page , described below. Settings swaps the menu for the list of settings: General , Shortcuts , Saving , Auto-redact , Secure screenshots , Strip and editor , Pro and Updates and about . Click one, or use the up and down arrow keys. The list is headed ‹ Settings : click it, or press Esc or Alt + Left , to go back to Home. A Search settings box above the list finds a setting by its name or what it says under it; press Enter or click a result and the window shows that section with the setting lit for a moment. See Settings sections . Manual opens this manual in your browser. It sits under the menu. When an update is waiting, a card appears with Update now . It restarts A9 Snap and takes a few seconds. At the bottom is the version and channel, for example v0.3.3 · Dev , with Up to date beside it when that is so, and a Check for updates icon (two circling arrows). Click it: the icon spins and the line says Checking… , then Up to date , or the card above appears. The icon is not in the Microsoft Store version, which Windows updates; there the version line has a Rate A9 Snap in the Microsoft Store link instead (see Rating A9 Snap in the Store ).

The middle Ready when you are reminds you of the hotkey and shows Running in the tray . Recent captures shows your six newest captures as thumbnails, with the file name, how long ago you took each, and a Volt dot on edited ones. Click one to open it in the editor. Open the strip shows more. With no captures yet it says where to start. Saving to shows your screenshots folder and Next file , the name the next capture will get. After a capture says what happens when you let go: Copied as an image , Copied as image and file , and Opens in the editor if you turned that on.

Quick capture The Quick capture row opens a page of seven tiles, four across and three below. Each tile is one button with a small picture of what it takes, its name, its keys and a line about it. Click a tile (or move to it with the arrow keys and press Enter ) and it starts that way of capturing, exactly as its keys do. Moving the focus with the arrows starts nothing. The Quick capture page. Without Pro the four Pro tiles carry a PRO badge. Region ( Alt + Z ): the picker, to drag a box. Window ( Alt + Z , then click): the picker, to click a window. Full screen ( Alt + Z , then F ): takes the screen the pointer is on at once, with no picker. Scrolling ( Alt + Z , then L ): the picker with L already on. Scrolling capture . Record video ( Alt + Z , then R ): the picker with R already on. Record video and GIF . Copy text ( Alt + X ): the picker for the OCR capture. It copies the text in a region and saves no picture. Secure capture ( Alt + Z , then S ): the picker with S already on. Secure capture . The keys on each tile are your own hotkeys: change one in Settings and the tile follows. The last four tiles are Pro features. Without Pro they carry a PRO badge, a click opens the Pro sheet for that feature (never a picker), and a row under the tiles says Four of these are part of A9 Snap Pro. with Get Pro, $14.99 . With Pro the badges and that row are gone. Under the tiles, Open recent captures opens the strip and shows its hotkey. The ? button, and F1 on this page, open Take a screenshot .

Delete a screenshot Point at a capture in Recent captures and a small red trash can appears in the top-right corner of its picture. It also shows when the capture has the keyboard focus. Click it, or press Delete with the capture focused, and: The capture fades out and the grid fills in with the next-newest one. A note at the bottom of the window says Deleted SNAP-0042.png with an Undo button, for 6 seconds. The file goes to the Recycle Bin, not away for good, and so does the hidden original the editor kept if you had edited it. Undo puts both back under the same names, exactly as they were, and the capture returns to the grid. Clicking the trash can never opens the editor. Next file doesn't change: a deleted capture keeps its number while A9 Snap is running, so the next capture is never given the number of the one you just threw away. If Windows can't move the file, for example because another app has it open, the capture stays and the note says why. The strip works the same way.

The ? buttons and F1 Every section, including Home, has a ? button at the top right. It opens the manual page for that section. Start at login has a small ? of its own. With the Home window in front, press F1 for the page that matches the section on screen. The tray menu's Manual item opens the front page.

The size of the window It opens at 1000 × 680 and can be made as small as 860 × 600. The left side never scrolls, whatever the size, with or without Pro and the update card; at the smallest size only the middle can.

Every setting, section by section, in the order the Home window lists them, with what each one does and its default. Every setting is in the Home window's list of settings: click Settings in the left-hand menu. The list is General , Shortcuts , Saving , Recording , Auto-redact , Secure screenshots , Strip and editor , Pro and Updates and about , and the Search settings box above it finds any setting by its name or by a word in what it says under it. Each section has a ? button at the top right that opens its manual page. A change is saved the moment you make it, and A9 Snap checks it. If a value is not allowed, a line under the setting says why and the setting goes back to what it was. For the window itself, see The Home window .

General The General section. Show a confirmation shows a small note at the bottom right after each capture, such as Copied · SNAP-0042.png . On by default. The note stays about a second and a half, or three and a half seconds when it has an Edit button. Problems always show, and stay for five seconds, whatever this setting says. Start at login starts A9 Snap in the tray when you sign in to Windows. On by default for a new install. See Start at login . Every on/off setting is a switch on the right, in the same place as the dropdowns.

Shortcuts The Shortcuts section. Capture hotkey starts a screenshot. Default Alt + Z . OCR capture hotkey copies recognized text from a region without saving a picture. Default Alt + X . It is a Pro feature: the row carries a PRO badge without Pro, and pressing the key opens the Pro sheet. Recent captures hotkey opens the strip . Default Alt + Shift + Z . Secure capture is shown, not set: the capture hotkey, then S in the picker (a Pro feature with a Pro badge; without Pro, pressing it opens the Pro sheet). Under the hotkeys a line lists the picker's keys: click a window, drag a region, F full screen, S secure (Pro), Esc cancel. To change a hotkey: Click the box. It says Press the keys… Press the combination you want, for example Ctrl + Alt + P . If the key is allowed and free, it is saved. Press Esc to leave the box without changing it. A hotkey needs Ctrl , Alt , Shift or Win with a key. Function keys and PrintScreen may stand alone. The three hotkeys must all be different. A9 Snap never takes Ctrl + Alt + S , Win + Shift + S or Ctrl + C , V , X and Z . They belong to Windows and to every app's editing keys. If another app already owns a key, the box is marked and a line says Alt+Z is taken by another app. Pick another. The tray icon also shows a warning badge until you fix it.

Saving The Saving section. Screenshots folder is where pictures are saved. Default Desktop\Screenshots . Browse… picks another, Open shows it, Use the default folder goes back. File name has Prefix (default SNAP- ) and Digits (default 4, from 0 to 6: how many digits the number has, padded with zeros; 0 means no padding). Change either one and new captures use it from the next one on; the number still comes from the folder, so it never restarts. Until you change one, A9 Snap follows the style of the files already in the folder, and a line says so. A line shows Next file , the real name. See Where screenshots go . Search inside screenshots (Pro) reads the words in each capture on this PC so the strip can find a capture by what is in it. On by default with Pro; without Pro the row shows a Pro badge and opens the Pro sheet. A line under it says how far the reading is ( Read 412 of 1,280 captures , then All captures read ), and Clear text index deletes the words read so far, after asking. The index holds text from your screenshots, in the hidden .a9snap folder in your screenshots folder, and never leaves this PC. Turning the setting off stops reading and deletes the index. Secure captures are never read. See Privacy . Remember which app each capture came from notes the app and window title of each new capture so the strip can search by them. On by default. Window titles can contain an email subject or a document's name; they stay in the hidden .a9snap folder in your screenshots folder and never leave this PC. Turning it off stops new notes and keeps the old ones; Clear next to it deletes them. See Privacy . Edit originals says how many untouched originals the editor has kept so Revert works and how much room they take ( 23 files, 41 MB ). They still hold anything you blurred. Clear asks first, then sends them to the Recycle Bin. After that Revert is gone for those captures; the edited pictures stay as they are and keep their Volt dot. Also copy as file puts the saved file on the clipboard next to the picture. Off by default. Tallest scrolling capture (Pro) is how tall a scrolling capture may get before it stops by itself: 10,000, 20,000 (the default) or 40,000 pixels. A very tall picture on a wide screen takes a lot of memory. Where screenshots go explains the numbering in full.

Recording The Recording section. The settings of recording , a Pro feature (without Pro the section and each row show a Pro badge, and pressing a row opens the Pro sheet). The two recording rows used to be under Saving. Highlight clicks draws a ring into the recording where you click, in your left or right colour, with a smaller ring on the pointer while you hold a button. The rings are in the video only, never on your screen. On for a new install; off if you recorded with an earlier version, until you turn it on. The preview under it shows how the rings look. See Click highlights . Left-click colour and Right-click colour are yellow and blue to start. Ring size is Small , Medium (the default) or Large . The rings follow your display scaling. Show the pointer in recordings draws the mouse pointer into a recording. On by default. Longest recording is how long a recording may run before it stops by itself: 1, 5, 10 (the default) or 30 minutes. The bar warns 10 seconds before.

Auto-redact The Auto-redact section, on mock data. The settings of Auto-redact , a Pro feature (without Pro the section and each row show a Pro badge, and pressing a row opens the Pro sheet; nothing is saved). Redact every capture before it's copied blurs private text in each new capture before it reaches the clipboard and your screenshots folder. Off by default. It adds a moment before the picture is on the clipboard (about a second for a full screen of text). The untouched original is kept in the hidden .a9snap folder, so Revert in the editor brings it back, and Clear on Edit originals (under Saving ) removes it. Secure captures are never redacted. What auto-redact blurs lists the built-in kinds: Email addresses , Phone numbers and Card numbers are on; IP addresses and Long key-like strings are off. The choice is used by this setting, Redact in the editor and Copy redacted in the strip. My patterns are your own: a name, an on/off switch and a Simple shape or an Advanced regular expression each, up to 100. Add a pattern or Add a starter (ticket numbers, employee IDs, account numbers). A pattern marked Too slow was skipped on a picture. See My patterns . Words to always hide holds up to 500 words or phrases, one per line, hidden as whole words ignoring case. Try it shows what your patterns and words would hide in text you type. Share with a team has Export… (a .a9redact file) and Import… , which lists a file before adding what is new. See Share with a team .

Secure screenshots The Secure screenshots section. The settings of secure capture , a Pro feature (without Pro the section shows a Pro badge and a click opens the Pro sheet). A9 Snap can start by itself when you sign in to Windows, so your hotkey is always ready. Here is how it behaves, and what to do when Windows says no. Start at login is on for a new install, in the downloaded version and the Microsoft Store version alike. A9 Snap starts straight into the tray: no window opens and nothing asks you anything. If you had turned it off before, it stays off.

The Microsoft Store version The Microsoft Store version starts at login through Windows' own startup task instead of a startup entry, because a Store app's startup entry would never reach Windows. It is on for a new install, the same as the downloaded version, but the Store doesn't launch the app for you: open A9 Snap once after installing , and that first launch switches the startup task on. Settings › Apps › Startup in Windows then shows A9 Snap with its switch on. The Start at login switch turns the task on and off. If you turn it off in Windows, A9 Snap says so and Fix in Windows opens that page, exactly as below; if an administrator's policy turned it off, the same line shows, and A9 Snap never tries to override either. A login start is quiet, as with the downloaded version: no window, only the tray icon. The restart recovery described at the bottom of this page works the same way in the Store version: the one-time task starts A9 Snap through its app execution alias ( a9snap.exe in your WindowsApps folder), because Task Scheduler can't start a Store app by the path of its program file.

Turn it on or off Open the Home window and choose Shortcuts . Use the Start at login switch. Turning it on adds a startup entry for your Windows user, with the program's path in quotes (the install folder has a space in it). Turning it off removes the entry.

What the switch shows The switch shows what Windows will really do, not only what you saved. Windows has its own list in Settings › Apps › Startup , and it can turn A9 Snap off there. If Windows turned it off, the switch stays on and a line under it says Windows has turned this off in Startup apps. Click Fix in Windows . It opens that Windows page. Turn A9 Snap on there. A9 Snap never switches Windows' own setting back on for you. If A9 Snap could not add its startup entry, the line says A9 Snap couldn't add itself to Windows startup. What you see when Windows has turned A9 Snap off in Startup apps.

It checks itself A9 Snap checks its startup entry every time it starts. If the entry is missing, has no quotes, points at another copy (an old path or a development build) or is out of date after an update, A9 Snap puts it right. If you switch the setting off, the entry is removed.

h: After Windows closes your apps for an update
t: After Windows closes your apps for an update Sometimes Windows closes every app so it can restart for an update, and then the restart never finishes, or you cancel it. Nothing signs you in again, so the startup entry never fires and A9 Snap would stay closed. To cover that, when Windows ends your session and Start at login is on, A9 Snap sets a one-time task in your own Task Scheduler named A9 Snap relaunch after Windows closed it . It starts A9 Snap again two minutes later and ends after an hour. If the PC really restarts, the startup entry starts A9 Snap and removes the task. Every start of A9 Snap removes the task. A9 Snap never holds up a shutdown or a restart, and it asks Windows to start it again after a crash. With Start at login off, no task is made.

Checking what happened The log file records how each run ended: quit from the tray, Windows ending the session (and whether the session is really ending), a crash, or a normal exit. A login start is recorded as started at login .

Fixes for the problems people hit most: a hotkey that does nothing, a picture that won't paste, a missing tray icon, and an update that fails. Find your problem below. If none of it helps, the log file says what A9 Snap did, and you can contact A9 Snap .

h: A hotkey is taken by another app
t: A hotkey is taken by another app What you see: pressing Alt + Z does nothing, the tray icon wears a warning badge, and Settings says Alt+Z is taken by another app. Pick another. Another program already owns that key, and Windows lets only one program have it. Open the Home window and choose Shortcuts . Click the box that is marked, then press a different combination, such as Ctrl + Alt + P . The same goes for OCR capture hotkey and Recent captures hotkey . If you would rather keep the key, close or reconfigure the other app first, then restart A9 Snap.

h: Nothing is on the clipboard, or it won't paste
t: Nothing is on the clipboard, or it won't paste Read the note. Copied · SNAP-0042.png means the picture is on the clipboard. Saved SNAP-0042.png · not copied gives the reason it was not. These notes show for five seconds, even with confirmations off. Try another app. Paste into Paint or a document. If it works there, the first app wants a file instead of a picture: turn on Also copy as file in Saving . Check a clipboard tool. A clipboard manager or a remote desktop session can hold the clipboard for a moment. Try again. Use the strip. Press Alt + Shift + Z , pick the capture and press Enter to copy it again as a picture plus its file.

h: OCR finds no text or cannot start
t: OCR finds no text or cannot start No text found means Windows could not read words in the selected picture. Try a tighter region around clear, upright text, or a larger region with less background. Your previous clipboard contents are unchanged. If the note says Windows OCR is unavailable for your profile's languages, install an OCR-capable language in Windows Settings under Time & language → Language & region , then try again. OCR is local. A9 Snap does not send the picture to an online service, so this does not require an account or an API key.

The picture wasn't saved The note says Copied · not saved with a reason, for example that the folder can't be written to or the disk is full. The picture is still on your clipboard, so paste it now. Then pick a folder you can write to in Saving .

The next number is wrong The number is the highest file in the folder plus one, counting only files named like your prefix. If you moved or deleted files, it follows the folder. See File names and numbering .

h: A9 Snap did not start after a restart
t: A9 Snap did not start after a restart Open the Home window (from the Start menu, if the tray icon is missing) and choose Shortcuts . Check that Start at login is on. If a line says Windows has turned this off in Startup apps. , click Fix in Windows and turn A9 Snap on there. If Windows closed your apps for an update and the restart never finished, A9 Snap starts again by itself two minutes later. See Start at login .

h: I can't find the tray icon
t: I can't find the tray icon Click the ^ arrow by the clock to show hidden icons. You can drag the Bullseye out onto the taskbar to keep it visible. If it isn't there, start A9 Snap from the Start menu.

h: Windows says it protected your PC
t: Windows says it protected your PC This happens with the installer from a9snap.com, not with the Microsoft Store version. The steps are on Install A9 Snap : click More info , then Run anyway .

An update failed The Home window's version line says Check failed , and the line under Version in Updates and about says why. Couldn't reach the update server. means your network, a firewall or a proxy blocked the check. The update didn't pass its signature check, so it was not installed. means the download was damaged or changed on the way, and A9 Snap refused it. Open Updates and about and click Check for updates again. A9 Snap checks on launch and every few hours, so a short outage fixes itself. Make sure your network or firewall allows raw.githubusercontent.com and github.com . See Privacy . If it still fails, download the installer again from a9snap.com and run it. It updates your copy and keeps your settings.

h: Alt+Z is slow to appear, or the screen freezes for a moment
t: Alt+Z is slow to appear, or the screen freezes for a moment A9 Snap times every capture. For each one it adds a line that starts with capture timing: to the log file . The line says how many milliseconds each step took, from the moment you pressed the hotkey to the moment the picker was on screen. When a capture takes longer than 300 milliseconds, a second line follows. It starts with slow capture: and names the slowest step. To see what happened at the time it stalled, open the log, search for slow capture , and look at the line closest to the time you noticed it. The step names are: grab is reading the screen. It takes longer on big monitors and on setups with several of them. windows is making the list of windows that a click can pick. secure is checking whether the window in front is on your Always secure list. layout is getting the picker windows ready. It is long when you plugged in or removed a monitor, or changed its size, since the last capture. post and paint are handing the picture to the picker and drawing it. A slow post means A9 Snap's own window thread was busy. show is putting the picker on screen. Two flags on the line help too: resumed=yes means the PC woke from sleep since the last capture, and unlocked=yes means you unlocked it. These lines hold timings only. They have times, picture sizes in pixels, screen scales and counts. They never have a picture, a window title, an app name or a file name, and for Always secure they say only whether the window in front matched ( yes or no ). They stay in the log on your PC. A9 Snap sends them nowhere.

Where the log file is A9 Snap writes a log to a9snap.log in this folder: %APPDATA%\ai.atlas9.a9snap\logs Press Win + R , paste that folder path and press Enter to open it. The log records starts and exits, hotkey conflicts, update checks, sizes, timings and the reasons for errors. It never contains the content of your screenshots. Your settings are in settings.json in the folder above it. If you installed A9 Snap from the Microsoft Store, Windows keeps those files inside the app's own folder instead. Press Win + R , type %LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages and press Enter , open the folder that starts with Atlas9LLC.A9Snap_ , then LocalCache\Roaming\ai.atlas9.a9snap\logs . Your screenshots are not there: they stay in your screenshots folder, whichever way you installed A9 Snap.

Contact A9 Snap Write to support@a9snap.com . Say what you were trying to do, what happened instead, and which version you have (it is at the bottom of the left-hand column in the Home window). A screenshot often helps. Check it for private details before you attach it. To suggest something new, choose Suggest a feature in the tray menu or open a9snap.com/feedback .

The app sends nothing beyond the update check and, only if you use Pro, its license check. No account, no telemetry in the app, no uploads. The website counts visits without cookies. A9 Snap is built to stay on your computer. This page lists everything it stores and everything it sends.

What leaves your PC Two things, and Free needs only the first. The update check, which the Microsoft Store version of A9 Snap does not even make: the Store updates it. See The update check . And, if you buy or enter a key for A9 Snap Pro , the license check. See The license check . A9 Snap has no account, no sign-in, no analytics and no crash reporting. It never uploads a screenshot anywhere.

The update check On launch and every few hours, A9 Snap asks one public file whether a newer version exists. The file is channels/dev.json or channels/stable.json , depending on your channel , at raw.githubusercontent.com in the A9 Snap releases repository on GitHub. If there is a newer version, A9 Snap downloads the installer from that same repository's releases and checks its signature before it will install anything. Those requests carry the normal information any web request does, such as your IP address. They carry no screenshot, no file name and no setting.

The license check Free never makes a license check. Pro does, and only after you press Get Pro , Enter key or Restore purchase , or once a key is on your PC: then A9 Snap asks the license server at a9voice.com whether the key is still good, when it starts and once a day, never in the middle of a capture. What a check sends: the product name ( a9snap-pro ); your license key, once you have one; an identifier for this PC, which is a one-way hash of the Windows machine ID. The machine ID itself is never sent; a label for this PC, such as PC 1a2b3c4d , made from that hash. It is never your computer's name; for Get Pro , the same identifier, so the payment can be matched to this PC. Stripe takes your card details and email on its own page; A9 Snap never sees them. Those requests carry the normal information any web request does, such as your IP address. They carry no screenshot, no file name, no window title and no setting. The server stores your email and the payment from the purchase, and the PCs a key is on. If your PC is offline, Pro keeps working for 30 days from the last good answer. A refunded key stops working at the next check.

Suggest a feature Suggest a feature (in the tray menu and on Updates and about ) sends nothing from your PC. It opens a9snap.com/feedback in your browser, and the only thing added to the address is your A9 Snap version number, as in ?v=0.17.1 . Nothing that identifies you or your PC, no screenshot, no file name and no setting goes with it. As with any web page, the server that hosts the site sees the request and your IP address. The page has no form, no visit count and no analytics. Its one button opens your own email app with the subject filled in. You write the email and you send it , and it holds only what you put in it, such as your email address and anything you attach.

h: What is stored on your PC
t: What is stored on your PC Screenshots go to the clipboard and to your screenshots folder, and nowhere else. Thumbnails for the strip and the Home window are made in memory and never written to disk. OCR (Copy text with Alt + X is a Pro feature) uses Windows' built-in recognizer on your PC. The picture goes to it in memory only, and the recognized text goes only to the clipboard when you ask for it. An OCR capture saves no PNG. There are no temporary image or text files and no recognized text in the log. Originals of edited captures are kept in a hidden .a9snap folder inside your screenshots folder. After a blur, the saved file has the pixels destroyed but the original still holds them. See Blur is permanent in the saved file . Delete .a9snap before you share the whole folder. Edit originals in Saving shows how many there are and clears them (to the Recycle Bin). Two small files of names and numbers sit beside them: floor.json (the highest number you deleted, so the next capture doesn't reuse it) and edited.json (which captures were edited, so the Volt dot stays after the originals are cleared). Which app each capture came from is noted in .a9snap\captures.json , in the same hidden folder next to the originals. For each new capture it holds the file name, size and time, the app's name (such as Google Chrome) and the window's title, so the strip can search by them. Window titles can contain an email subject or a document's name. The notes stay in your screenshots folder, never leave this PC and never go into the log. Turn them off with Remember which app each capture came from in Saving , and press Clear there to delete what is already noted. Delete .a9snap before you share the whole folder. A secure capture never notes them. Auto-redact (Pro) reads a picture with Windows' built-in recognizer on your PC, in memory, to find email addresses, phone numbers, card numbers and your own patterns and words, and blurs them. What it finds is never written to the log (the log says only how many items were blurred or patterns skipped, and how long it took), is never sent anywhere and is not kept: the blurred areas are pixels in the picture. Your patterns and words ( My patterns and Words to always hide ) are kept with your other settings in settings.json on this PC and are never logged or sent; they leave this PC only in a .a9redact file you save with Export… , which is plain text that anyone you give it to can read. With Redact every capture before it's copied on, the untouched original of each capture is kept in .a9snap like an edit's, and it still holds what was blurred: Clear on Edit originals in Saving removes them, and you should delete .a9snap before you share the whole folder. See Auto-redact . The words in your captures (Pro, Search inside screenshots ) are kept in .a9snap\text.json , in the same hidden folder next to the originals and captures.json . A9 Snap reads each capture with Windows' built-in recognizer on your PC, in memory, and the index holds the file name, size and time of each capture and the text found in it, so the strip can search by it. The index holds text from your screenshots , including anything on them that you would not want shared. It stays in your screenshots folder, never leaves this PC and never goes into the log (the log says only how many pictures were read and how long it took). Press Clear text index in Saving to delete it, or turn Search inside screenshots off, which stops reading and deletes it. Delete .a9snap before you share the whole folder. A secure capture is never read or indexed. Without Pro nothing is read. Recordings (Pro, press R in the picker) are MP4 files in your screenshots folder, numbered with your pictures, and a GIF made from one is saved next to it. A9 Snap never uploads one. Sound is recorded only when you turn it on : the microphone and your PC's sound are off by default and the recording bar's switches turn them on and off, and a device that is switched off is closed. The app and window title of a recording are noted like a picture's ( captures.json ), and nothing of what was on screen or what was said is read or logged: the log says only how long a recording was and how big. A secure capture is never recorded, and the text index and auto-redact do not read recordings. See Record video and GIF . Click highlights (Pro, Highlight clicks in Settings, Recording) draw rings into a recording where you click. A9 Snap watches the mouse only while such a recording runs, and uses only where and when the left or right button was pressed inside the recorded area, and where the pointer went while it was held there. That is used to draw the rings into the video and is not written anywhere else, kept or sent. No keys are captured. The log says only whether highlights were on. Secure captures (Pro, press S in the picker) go to the clipboard and, unless you chose Clipboard only , to a folder of their own, %LOCALAPPDATA%\A9 Snap\Secure by default (on the Microsoft Store version Windows keeps that folder inside the app's own AppData; Open in the settings shows the real one). The folder is hidden and marked not to be content-indexed, so Windows Search and Explorer's thumbnail cache leave it alone. The copy on the clipboard carries the formats that keep it out of Windows' clipboard history and the cloud clipboard. A secure capture is never in the strip, the Home window, search, captures.json , the text index or your screenshots folder's numbering, notes no app or window, and never opens the editor. The log says only "secure capture saved", with the size and timing, never a file name. Clear the secure folder deletes for good, not to the Recycle Bin, and Clear the clipboard after empties the clipboard only while it still holds the secure picture. With the Secure vault on (Pro, off by default), new secure captures are written to that folder encrypted, as .a9vault files, and never as a PNG: AES-256-GCM, with a key of its own for each file, locked with your Windows account (DPAPI) before it is stored. The key is tied to your Windows account : if that account or its profile is lost or reset, or the files are moved to another PC or Windows user, they can't be opened again and A9 Snap can't recover them. Opening the vault asks Windows Hello (or your Windows sign-in); it shows thumbnails decrypted in memory only, locks after 2 minutes unused or when the PC locks, and Delete overwrites and removes a file for good. Nothing is sent anywhere, and the log says only how many files, never a name. Always secure for these apps keeps a list of programs (their exe paths and names) in A9 Snap's settings; nothing about a secure capture is written to captures.json . Without the vault a secure capture is not encrypted. If you point the secure folder at a OneDrive, Dropbox or other synced folder, that service uploads what is in it; the settings warn you. A9 View (free: double-click a picture or a video, or Open with , then A9 Snap ) reads the picture or video and the names of the other files in its folder, and writes nothing about them: no thumbnail or video frame (the thumbnail strip is drawn from memory and never saved), no list of what you looked at, no index. A video is read from disk a piece at a time through A9 Snap's own local route, with no network call, and nothing is held open between pieces, so the file is free the moment it stops playing. Save this frame writes a file only when you ask. Nothing it shows goes into the search index, which stays in your screenshots folder and covers captures only. A9 View never opens a secure capture or the vault, makes no network call, and the log says only a picture's type, size and timing, never a name. Its info panel reads the camera data stored in a picture (camera, lens, exposure, date taken, place) and shows it to you; if there is a place, Open in maps builds a map link from those coordinates and opens it in your browser only when you click it . That click is the only way anything about a picture leaves your PC, and A9 Snap sends nothing itself. Rename ( F2 ) and Save a copy are the only things that write a file, and only when you ask. Windows' list of what can open pictures gets entries for A9 Snap when you install it, and loses them when you uninstall. E edits a picture in the same window: a capture is saved the way the editor saves it (over itself, with its untouched original kept in the hidden .a9snap folder inside your screenshots folder), and any other picture is never changed : saving writes a copy next to it ( name (edited) ), or the next numbered capture in your screenshots folder, and that file is the only thing written (no kept original, thumbnail, edit mark or search text for a picture that is not a capture). A copy carries no camera or location data. If you pick Keep my size and place , the window's size and place are kept in viewer-window.json next to the settings. See A9 View . The Store rating card (only the Microsoft Store version) goes by two plain counts kept in rating.json beside your settings: the day you first started A9 Snap, and how many captures you have taken, with the time of the last one and whether the card was shown or answered. They never leave your PC and are never sent anywhere. The log says only that the card was shown or how it was answered. The version you install from a9snap.com keeps none of this. See Rating A9 Snap in the Store . Settings are in settings.json in %APPDATA%\ai.atlas9.a9snap . A Pro key, if you have one, is kept beside it in pro-license.json . Scrolling captures (Pro, press L in the picker) are ordinary pictures: they go to the clipboard and your screenshots folder like any capture (or where a secure capture goes, with S ). A9 Snap looks only at the area you chose, keeps the frames in memory while it stitches them and never uploads anything. The log says how many frames there were and how big the picture is, never what was in it. See Scrolling capture . Backgrounds (Pro: the editor's Background and Share-ready) are drawn on your PC when you save, and the finished picture is the only thing written. The style you used last (its padding, colours, corner size, shadow and shape) is kept in settings.json next to your other settings so Share-ready can use it again. Nothing is sent anywhere. See Backgrounds . Ready to send (A9 View) and, with Pro, batch and side by side run on your PC. They read the picture, and write only the file you ask for: next to the original, as a new capture, into a ready folder, or onto the clipboard. The original is never changed, nothing is uploaded, no list of the pictures you made ready is kept, and the log never names a file or folder. Remove location and camera details (on to begin with) writes the new file without the location , camera , lens , date taken and other tags (software, owner, copyright, comments, text notes and the like) that the original carried; the picture is turned the right way up first. The one thing carried over is the colour profile, which says what the colours mean and holds none of those. The choices you used last are kept in settings.json . See Ready to send . Requests from other apps. An app on your PC that is made to work with A9 Snap, such as A9 Voice, can ask it for a picture (see Other A9 apps ). You take the picture in A9 Snap's picker, and it is saved like any capture. A9 Snap then writes a small answer file where that app asks, which has to be a folder inside your own AppData: whether the picture was saved, cancelled, busy or timed out and, when saved, where the picture is. It writes nothing for a request that points anywhere else, never replaces a file that isn't an earlier answer, and makes no folder. What the app does with the picture after that is up to that app. A9 Snap keeps its own copy as with any capture, and a picture of an app on your Always secure list is never handed out. Nothing is sent over the network, and the log says only that a request came in and how it ended, never a file name or folder. Share (Pro: the Share button on the confirmation, H or Share… in the strip, Share in the editor) opens Windows' own Share sheet on a capture. A9 Snap gives Windows the file (and the picture, for apps that take one) and makes no network call, holds no account and keeps no list of targets; the app you pick takes it from there. The log says only that the sheet opened and for how many files, never a name. See Share to your apps . The log is in the logs folder beside it. It records sizes, timings and status codes, never the content of a screenshot, a file or recognized text. Start at login adds one startup entry for your Windows user, and a one-time Task Scheduler task when Windows ends your session. See Start at login .

This website The app and this website are separate. The app sends nothing beyond the update check and, for Pro, the license check above. Nothing on this page changes that. The website counts how it is used, without cookies and without anything that identifies you (the feedback page is left out of all of it): Visits and where they came from. When you open a page, the site's own script remembers, for that browser tab only, the campaign tags on the link you followed (such as utm_source ), the address of the site that sent you (the host name only, never the full address) and the first page you landed on. It sends that to the license server at a9voice.com once per visit, so the count says, for example, "12 visits from a link tagged newsletter". It stores nothing on your PC beyond that tab's memory, which goes away when you close the tab, and it sets no cookie. Download clicks. The Download the installer button on Install A9 Snap goes through the same server, which counts the click with the same tags and then sends you on to the installer. A click on the Microsoft Store badge is counted the same way, and the badge's link carries a campaign name (such as newsletter , or direct ) so the Store can tell its own installs apart. A cookieless page count. The site also uses Cloudflare Web Analytics, which counts page views without cookies. None of these counts stores your IP address, and none can tell you apart from anyone else who came the same way. They carry no screenshot, no setting and nothing from the app. The manual's fonts and scripts come from a9snap.com. The home page loads its fonts from Google Fonts and reads the newest version number from the same GitHub file that the app uses.

How A9 Snap finds and installs new versions, and what the Dev and Stable channels mean. A9 Snap updates itself, but never without you. It checks, downloads in the background, and then waits for you to restart.

The Microsoft Store version If you installed A9 Snap from the Microsoft Store, Windows updates it and A9 Snap does not check for updates itself. There is no Check for updates button, no Update now card, no channel and no update item in the tray menu. Updates and about says Updates come from the Microsoft Store. , and the version line shows your version with Microsoft Store , for example v0.3.6 · Microsoft Store . To look now, open the Microsoft Store, then Library and Get updates . Everything below is about the version you install from a9snap.com.

h: Rating A9 Snap in the Store
t: Rating A9 Snap in the Store The Store version has two ways to rate it, and nothing else about it sends anything. Beside the version in the left-hand column and on Updates and about is Rate A9 Snap in the Microsoft Store . It is always there: click it and Windows' own rating dialog opens (or, if Windows can't show it, the Store's review page for A9 Snap). After at least 7 days of use and at least 20 captures, the Home window also shows one small card: Enjoying A9 Snap? A rating in the Microsoft Store helps other people find it. with three buttons. Rate opens the same dialog and the card never comes back. Not now hides the card and asks once more after 30 days, then never. Don't ask again hides it for good. The card is only ever inside the Home window. It does not appear while you are capturing or in the 10 minutes after a capture, and it is never a pop-up over other apps. The copy you installed from a9snap.com never shows it. The days and the capture count it goes by stay on your PC; see Privacy .

How an update works A9 Snap checks on launch and every few hours. You can check now with the Check for updates icon (two circling arrows) after the version number at the bottom of the left-hand column, with Check for updates in Updates and about , or in the tray menu. The icon spins and the line says Checking… , then Up to date ; if a newer version exists the card appears. The icon is off while a check or a download runs. If a newer version exists, it downloads it and checks its signature. The Home window shows a card: Downloading 0.3.3… , then Version 0.3.3 is ready . The tray menu says Restart to update to 0.3.3 . Click Update now on the card, or choose the tray item. A9 Snap restarts. It takes a few seconds, and your settings and screenshots are untouched. If you ignore the card, nothing happens. The update waits until you are ready. A failed check never throws away an update that is already downloaded.

Dev and Stable The channel decides which versions you are offered. Dev gets every build. It is the default, and it is how new features reach you first. Stable gets only the builds that were promoted after they had time to prove themselves. To switch, open Updates and about and pick the other one in Update channel . The version line at the bottom left of the Home window shows your channel, for example v0.3.3 · Dev . Switching to Stable never installs an older version. It just waits for the next promoted build.
See what changed Release notes in Updates and about opens your version's notes on GitHub. What's new lists every version in this manual.

Suggest a feature Choose Suggest a feature in the tray menu, or open Updates and about and click Open the page on the Suggest a feature row. Your browser opens a9snap.com/feedback . The page says what helps in a suggestion and has one button, Email your suggestion , which opens your email app with the subject filled in. You write the message and send it yourself. A9 Snap sends nothing. The link it opens carries your version number and nothing else, so the subject can read, for example, A9 Snap suggestion (0.17.1) . See Privacy .
If an update fails See An update failed .
