A secure capture goes to the clipboard and a folder of its own, and nowhere else. It stays out of the strip, the Home window, Windows' clipboard history and Windows Search. The Secure vault keeps those files encrypted, and Always secure makes chosen apps secure for you. It is a Pro feature. Some pictures should not end up in your screenshots folder, the strip, Windows' clipboard history or a folder that syncs to the cloud: a password, a bank page, a private message. Secure capture is for those. It is part of A9 Snap Pro: see Pro features .

Take a secure capture There are three ways to start one, and they all end in the same picker. From the keyboard. Press Alt + Z . Tap S . A padlock appears on the outline, and the size says Secure , for example Secure · 600 × 400 . Click a window, press F for the whole screen, or drag a region, as you always do. From the sidebar. With Pro on, the Home window has a Secure capture button under Capture , with Alt+Z, S on it. It opens the picker with secure already on, so skip step 2. With Pro on, the Secure capture button sits under Capture. From the tray. With Pro on, the tray menu has Secure capture under Capture region . It does the same. If you changed the capture hotkey, the keys follow it: your hotkey, then S . The Shortcuts page lists them too, and the picker's hint line says S secure . The first time Pro turns on, the hint comes back for your next 5 captures. Tap S again to turn it off. It is never sticky: the next capture starts as a normal one. The toast says Secure · copied (or Secure · copied · saved ) with a padlock. It shows no thumbnail and no Edit button, and clicking it does nothing, so it cannot lead to the strip. Without Pro there is no Secure capture button in the sidebar and no item in the tray, and S does not switch secure on. The picker says Secure capture is part of A9 Snap Pro , and the capture is a normal one. When the picker closes, the Pro sheet opens once, then stays out of your way until the next time you start A9 Snap.

Where it goes The clipboard , with the formats that keep it out of Windows' clipboard history ( Win + V ) and the cloud clipboard. With Also copy as file on and a file saved, the file's path rides along too. The secure folder , unless you chose Clipboard only . The default is %LOCALAPPDATA%\A9 Snap\Secure , which is not synced. Files are numbered inside that folder only, with the same prefix and digits as your screenshots, so your screenshots folder's numbering and Next file never move. The secure folder is hidden and marked as not to be content-indexed, so Windows Search and Explorer's thumbnail cache leave it alone. Use Open in the settings below to see it.

h: What a secure capture never does
t: What a secure capture never does It never appears in the strip , in the Home window's recent captures, in search or in the app chips. It never notes which app or window it came from. It never opens the editor, even with Open the editor after every capture on. Editing a secure capture is not possible, because the editor keeps originals in the screenshots folder. The log says "secure capture saved" and the size and timing, and never a file name.

Secure vault By default a secure capture is an ordinary PNG in the secure folder, which anyone at your PC can open. The Secure vault keeps it encrypted instead. In Settings > Secure screenshots , turn on Encryption for the secure folder . It is off by default. The Secure vault is the secure folder with encryption on, not a second place. Take secure captures as usual. They are written as .a9vault files, never as a PNG, so Explorer and Windows Search only ever see encrypted files. The clipboard copy at the moment you capture is unchanged: it still stays out of Windows' clipboard history and the cloud clipboard. If secure PNGs are already in the folder when you turn it on, A9 Snap asks under the switch: Encrypt the N secure pictures already in the folder? Encrypt and delete the PNGs encrypts each one and then deletes the PNG for good. You can choose Not now . Until they are encrypted, the row and the vault window say N pictures in the secure folder aren't encrypted yet , with Encrypt now . Each file has a key of its own, and that key is locked with your Windows account (DPAPI) before it is stored, so the file opens only for you, on this PC. The encryption is AES-256-GCM, so a file that was changed, even by one byte, refuses to open.

Open the vault With encryption on, the Vault button in the left-hand column (it reads Secure and opens the folder in Explorer when encryption is off), Open on the Secure folder row, the Secure vault row on the Pro page, or Secure vault in the tray menu (Pro) open the vault. Windows asks first: Windows Hello (face, fingerprint or PIN), or the Windows sign-in , if Hello isn't set up on this PC. The vault window shows a thumbnail of each file, decrypted in memory only, with: Copy. The picture goes on the clipboard, kept out of Windows' clipboard history and the cloud clipboard, and cleared by Clear the clipboard after if you set it. Export as PNG. A Save dialog asks where. The file you save there is an ordinary PNG, and yours to look after. Delete. Asks first, then deletes for good : the file is overwritten and removed, not sent to the Recycle Bin. The vault locks itself after 2 minutes without use, when you lock your PC ( Win + L ) and when you close the window; locking closes the window. Opening it again asks Windows again. Esc or Lock now locks it at once. If PNGs are still in the secure folder, a line at the top of the vault says N pictures in the secure folder aren't encrypted yet with Encrypt now , and the vault only says it is empty when the folder holds no pictures at all. Clear the secure folder and Empty now work on vault files too, and delete them for good.

h: If you lose your Windows account
t: If you lose your Windows account The key of each file is tied to your Windows account. If that account is deleted or its profile is reset, or you move the files to another PC or another Windows user, the vault files can't be opened again, and A9 Snap can't get them back. Export the pictures you need as PNGs first. A password reset that keeps your profile is fine; a reinstall of Windows that doesn't is not.

Always secure for chosen apps Some apps should never be one forgotten key press away from your screenshots folder: a password manager, a bank, a private chat. List them and A9 Snap makes the capture secure for you. In Settings > Secure screenshots , find Always secure for these apps and press Add app . Pick an app you have captured before, an app with a window open now, or choose Browse… for an .exe . Press Remove next to an app to take it off the list. From then on, a capture whose source belongs to a listed app starts in secure mode. The source is the same one a capture notes: the window you clicked, the window in front when you take the whole screen ( F ), or the window under the middle of a region you drag. Before you let go, the picker's size line says Secure and the app's name, for example Secure · Password Manager · 640 × 480 , and the padlock shows. Press S to take that one capture normally instead; S again puts it back. On any other app S still turns secure on, as always. Apps are told apart by the program, not by the window's title, so a window that renames itself is still the same app. If you press R to record, the recording goes ahead: the list applies to pictures. The list is kept in A9 Snap's settings. Nothing about a secure capture is written to captures.json or anywhere else.

Settings Open Settings in the Home window and choose Secure screenshots (its ? opens this page). Without Pro the section, and the Secure capture row on the Shortcuts page, show a Pro badge, and clicking either opens the Pro sheet. Where secure captures go. Secure folder (the default) or Clipboard only , which writes no file anywhere. Secure folder. The one place secure pictures live; the vault is this folder with encryption on. Browse… chooses another folder, but not your screenshots folder. A folder under OneDrive, Dropbox or another synced folder shows This folder is synced to the cloud; secure captures would be uploaded , because they would be. Open shows the folder in Explorer (with encryption on it opens the vault, the same as the Secure / Vault button in the left-hand column), and on the Microsoft Store version it shows the real folder, even though Windows keeps that version's AppData in its own place. Empty now asks first, in the window. Clear the secure folder. Never , When A9 Snap quits , After 1 hour , After 24 hours or After 7 days . A picture that came due while A9 Snap was closed is cleared the next time it starts. Secure pictures are deleted for good, not to the Recycle Bin. This is the one place A9 Snap deletes without a way back, because a Recycle Bin copy would defeat the point. It only clears a folder it made itself, and only .png and .a9vault files directly in it: choose a folder that already holds other files and A9 Snap uses it but never clears it. Encryption for the secure folder. See Secure vault . A line under it says how many encrypted pictures the folder holds, or how many are not encrypted yet, with Encrypt now . Always secure for these apps. See Always secure for chosen apps . Clear the clipboard after. Off (the default), 30 seconds , 1 minute or 5 minutes . A9 Snap clears the clipboard only if it still holds the secure picture. Anything you copied since is never cleared.

What it does not do Without the Secure vault, a secure capture is not encrypted and not locked away: anyone who can open your Windows account can open the secure folder. It keeps a picture out of the places that would otherwise keep it, and it can delete it for you on a schedule. With the vault on, the files are encrypted for your Windows account, but anyone who is signed in as you can still ask for them, and the vault asks Windows Hello (or your sign-in) each time. A picture you export, or paste somewhere, is no longer protected. See Privacy .

Auto-redact finds email addresses, phone numbers, card numbers and your own patterns and words in a picture and blurs them, so you can send it without a second look at every line. It is a Pro feature, and it reads the picture on your PC. Screenshots catch more than you meant them to: an email address in a corner, a phone number in a signature, an employee ID in a header, a customer's name in a ticket. Auto-redact is part of A9 Snap Pro . It reads the words in the picture with the same Windows text recognition that Copy text and Alt+X use, finds the ones that look like private details, and the ones you taught it, and blurs them. Nothing is uploaded: the reading happens on your PC.

What it finds Email addresses , such as ana.lee+news@mail.example.co.uk . Phone numbers in the usual North American writings, (555) 123-4567 , 555-123-4567 , 555.123.4567 , 1 555 123 4567 , and international numbers that start with a plus, +44 20 7183 8750 . A number split across words is still one number. Card numbers : 13 to 19 digits that pass the card check, written together or in groups split by spaces or dashes. Your own patterns and words . Two more are in the list and off until you turn them on under Auto-redact in Settings: IP addresses and long key-like strings (a long run of letters and digits with no spaces, the shape of an access key). Look-alikes are left alone: a date such as 2024-10-31 , a version such as 1.2.3 , an order number, a sum, a number that fails the card check. A phone number must be written with a space, dash, dot or bracket, or start with a plus, so a plain run of ten digits (an id, a time stamp) is not blurred as a phone number. Windows has to read the text correctly for A9 Snap to find it. Small, blurry or stylised text may be missed, and a misread digit can turn a card number into one that fails the check. Look at the picture before you send it. Auto-redact is a safety net, not a guarantee.

In the editor Open a capture in the editor , or press E on a picture in A9 View , and press R or click Redact in the top bar. A9 Snap reads the picture and puts a Blur over every match, a few pixels larger than the words. A line under the toolbar says what it did: Blurred 3 items: 2 emails, Employee IDs. When nothing is found it says Nothing to redact found. , and pressing it again on a picture that is already blurred says Already blurred. At the top right of the picture, the Hidden list shows each thing that was blurred and what found it: Email address , Phone number , the name of your pattern, or Word list . Click a line to pick that blur and see where it is. If one is a wrong match, press Undo beside it: that blur goes and the others stay. Ctrl + Z brings it back. The blurs are ordinary Blur shapes. You can select one, move it, resize it, delete it with Delete , or undo the whole Redact with Ctrl + Z , and you can add your own. A blur is real pixelation: once you save, the file holds flat blocks where the text was. See Blur is permanent in the saved file . Without Pro the Redact button shows a Pro badge and opens the Pro sheet.

In the strip Right-click a capture in the strip and choose Copy redacted . A blurred copy of the picture goes on the clipboard, ready to paste. The file is not changed. The note says Copied redacted · 3 blurred , or Copied · nothing to redact found when there was nothing to blur (the picture is then copied as it is). Without Pro the item shows a Pro badge and opens the Pro sheet.

Redact every capture Turn on Redact every capture before it's copied under Auto-redact in Settings and every new capture is read and blurred before it reaches the clipboard and your screenshots folder. It is off by default, and it needs Pro. It adds a moment. The picture is on the clipboard only once Windows has read it: about a second for a full screen of text, a fraction of that for a small region. A capture with nothing to blur is copied as it is. Your patterns and words add very little to that. The untouched original is kept , in the hidden .a9snap folder next to your screenshots, like an edit's original. Open the capture in the editor and Revert brings it back; Clear on the Edit originals row in Saving removes it, after which the capture can no longer be reverted. The capture shows the Volt dot of an edited one. Delete .a9snap before you share the whole folder. A wrong match: open the capture in the editor, press Revert to get the untouched picture back, then press R . The Hidden list shows what matched; press Undo beside the wrong one and save. If Windows can't read the picture (no text recognition language is installed, say), the capture is copied and saved as it is, and the note says couldn't check for private text . If a pattern was skipped because it was too slow, the note says so: 1 pattern skipped (too slow) . See Limits . Secure captures are never redacted. They stay out of the strip and the screenshots folder already, and they are never read. What auto-redact blurs in the same section chooses the built-in kinds, for this setting, Redact in the editor and Copy redacted in the strip. Your patterns have their own on/off switches.

My patterns Every workplace has private text of its own: employee IDs, ticket and case numbers, account numbers, project codes. Add them under Settings › Auto-redact , in My patterns , and Auto-redact hides them everywhere it runs, in the same way as the built-in kinds. Each pattern has a name, an on/off switch, and one of two kinds: Simple describes the shape of the text. # is any digit, A any letter and * any letter or digit; everything else means itself. EMP-###### is EMP- and six digits; INC####### is INC and seven digits; AA-## is two letters, a dash and two digits. To mean a real # , A or * , put a backslash before it: \A is the letter A, so \ACME-#### finds ACME numbers. A Simple pattern matches a whole thing: EMP-###### doesn't match inside EMP-0044177 . Advanced is a regular expression, such as \bPRJ-\d{4}\b . Use \b to keep a match from sitting inside a longer word. Look-ahead, look-behind and back-references aren't supported. An expression that isn't valid shows why, and can't be saved. Two options: Ignore case (on to start): emp-123 and EMP-123 are the same. Allow spaces or dashes inside (off to start): for text that gets read with a gap in it. With it on, EMP-###### also finds EMP 00 44 17 . As with every match, whole words are blurred: if a pattern matches part of a word, the whole word goes.

Starters Add a starter puts a ready pattern in your list, switched on, for you to change as you like: Ticket numbers: INC , RITM , REQ , CHG or TASK followed by seven digits. Employee IDs: EMP- or E followed by five to eight digits. Account numbers: eight to twelve digits in a row. Dates written without separators, such as 20261031 , are eight digits too: turn this one off if you don't want them blurred.

Words to always hide For names that have no shape, such as a customer or a project code name, type them under Words to always hide , one word or phrase per line, and press Save (leaving the box saves too). Each is hidden wherever it stands as a whole word, ignoring case: Heron hides heron and (Heron's) , but not Heronry . A phrase is found when its words are on the same line.

Try it Type or paste some text into Try it , under the words. The box shows which patterns and words match and what they would hide, as you type, including the pattern you are still editing. Nothing there is saved.

Share with a team Export… saves your patterns and words to a .a9redact file, which is plain JSON you can read. Send it to a colleague any way you like: A9 Snap sends nothing. Import… opens such a file and first lists what it holds and what will happen: entries already in your list are skipped, one that can't be used says so, and Add adds the rest. Importing the same file twice adds nothing.

Limits Up to 100 patterns and 500 words . Each pattern gets 50 milliseconds per picture. One that runs over is skipped for that picture, the note after the capture or in the editor says so, and the pattern is marked Too slow in your list until you change it or switch it off and on. Make it simpler: fewer repeats, and less that is optional.
Privacy Patterns and words are kept with your other settings on this PC. They are never sent anywhere, and the log records only how many, never a pattern, a word or what matched. See Privacy .

Without Pro Without Pro, Redact and Copy redacted show a Pro badge and open the Pro sheet, and the Auto-redact settings, My patterns and the rest, show the badge; pressing them opens the Pro sheet and saves nothing. Nothing is read and the license is not checked: a free copy never makes one.

Record a window, a region or a whole screen as an MP4, with a ring around every click, then paste it like a picture. A short recording can become a GIF. It is a Pro feature. Some things are easier to show than to screenshot: a click path, a bug that only happens when you hover. Video and GIF capture records what you choose to a small MP4 file, puts the file on the clipboard so it pastes into a chat or an email as an attachment, and keeps it next to your screenshots. It is part of A9 Snap Pro: see Pro features .

Record something Press Alt + Z . Press R . The size says Record , for example Record · 1280 × 720 . (You can also press R after you start dragging, or just before you let go.) Click a window, press F for the whole monitor, or drag a region, as you always do. Recording starts the moment you let go. If you changed the capture hotkey, the keys follow it: your hotkey, then R . The picker's hint line says R record (Pro) . R is never sticky: the next capture starts as a normal picture. R and S (secure capture) do not go together in this version. Press one while the other is on and the picker says so. Without Pro, R does not record. The picker says Video capture is part of A9 Snap Pro , the capture is a normal picture, and the Pro sheet opens once after the picker closes.

While it records A small bar sits just outside the area you chose, on the same monitor (inside its bottom edge when the area fills the screen). It has a Volt dot, the time, and: Pause and Resume. Paused time is left out of the video. Stop. Or press Alt + Z again, whichever window has the keyboard. The microphone and PC sound switches. Both are off until you turn them on, and A9 Snap remembers your choice. PC sound is whatever your speakers are playing. A thin Volt outline marks the recorded area. Neither the outline nor the bar is ever in the video. Press Esc while the bar has the keyboard (or while the pointer is on it) and it asks Discard recording? , with Discard and Keep recording . A recording stops by itself after 10 minutes, with a warning 10 seconds before ( Stops in 9 s on the bar). Change that under Longest recording in Settings: 1, 5, 10 or 30 minutes.

Click highlights In a recording, a click is easy to miss. With Highlight clicks on, A9 Snap draws a ring where you click, so people watching can see what you pressed. A click shows a ring around the pointer that grows a little and fades in about half a second. Left and right clicks have their own colours: yellow for left and blue for right, unless you choose others. A double-click shows two quick rings. Holding a button down keeps a smaller ring on the pointer until you let go, so a drag can be followed. The rings are drawn into the video and nowhere else. Nothing appears on your screen while you record, and other apps never see them. They are in the GIF made from a recording, and they stay through Trim . They follow your display scaling, so they look the same size on a screen at 100% and one at 150%. Only clicks inside the area you are recording are shown. A click outside it, a click on the recording bar and a click while the recording is paused are left out. If you drag out of the area, the ring is hidden until the pointer comes back. The middle button and the wheel make no rings, and keys are never shown. Highlight clicks is on for a new install. If you recorded with an earlier version, it starts off so your videos look as before, and the note after your next recording tells you where to turn it on. A9 Snap watches the mouse only while a recording with highlights is running. It uses where and when you clicked inside the area to draw the rings, and keeps none of it: nothing about a click is written anywhere except into the video. See Privacy . Windows doesn't tell an ordinary app about clicks in an app that is running as administrator, so those clicks get no ring.

What you get A file, in the same numbering as your pictures. The next number in your screenshots folder, ending in .mp4 : if the last picture was SNAP-0042.png , the recording is SNAP-0043.mp4 , and the next picture is SNAP-0044.png . See Where screenshots go . On the clipboard as a file , so Ctrl + V attaches it in a chat or an email. A toast that says Recording saved · copied as file , with Save as GIF (for a recording up to 30 seconds), Show in folder and Share (the Windows Share sheet; see Share to your apps ). Clicking the toast opens the strip on it. The video is H.264 at 30 frames a second, made with your graphics card's encoder when it has one. If the area is taller than 1080 pixels it is scaled down to 1080 lines, keeping its shape. The mouse pointer is in the video (turn that off with Show the pointer in recordings in Settings).

Make a GIF Press Save as GIF on the toast, or right-click the recording in the strip and choose Save as GIF . A9 Snap writes a GIF next to the recording with the next number, copies it as a file and says so. It is 15 frames a second, never wider than 960 pixels, with a palette chosen for that clip. A recording longer than 30 seconds can't become a GIF. A longer clip takes longer to convert, because every frame has to be decoded twice (once to choose the palette): a few seconds for a short region on a typical PC, and a minute or more for 30 seconds of a full 1080p screen on a slow one. Making the GIF… stays on screen until it is done.

h: In the strip and the Home window
t: In the strip and the Home window A recording's card shows its first frame, a play badge and its length. Press Enter or double-click to play it in A9 View (or, with Open my recordings in A9 View off in Settings, your default player). Clicking the note after a recording does the same. Ctrl + C , dragging it out, Delete and Undo work as they do for a picture; Copy puts the file on the clipboard. Search finds a recording by its name and by the app and window title noted when it started. The editor does not open recordings, and Secure capture, Auto-redact and search inside pictures do not apply to them in this version.

Settings Open Recording in the Home window's list of settings. The Recording section. Highlight clicks. On for a new install. A small preview under it shows the rings in your colours and size. Left-click colour and Right-click colour. Click a colour to choose another. Ring size. Small, Medium (the default) or Large. Show the pointer in recordings. On by default. Longest recording. 1, 5, 10 (the default) or 30 minutes. The microphone and PC sound switches are on the recording bar.

Privacy Recording happens on your PC and the files stay there: A9 Snap never uploads a recording. Sound is recorded only when you turn it on : the microphone and PC sound are off by default, and switching one off closes it. For click highlights, only clicks inside the recorded area are used, only while it records, and no keys are captured. The log says how long a recording was, its size and whether highlights were on, never what was on screen or where anyone clicked. See Privacy .

If it doesn't work "The screen sent no picture to record." A locked PC or a protected screen has nothing to capture. Unlock it and try again. No rings in the video. Check Highlight clicks under Recording in Settings. Clicks in an app running as administrator get none. If the bar says Clicks can't be highlighted , the recording goes on without them. A sound switch turns itself off and the bar names the problem: no microphone, no sound output, or Windows blocking the microphone ( Settings > Privacy & security > Microphone , which has to allow desktop apps). A recording that was running when you quit A9 Snap is finished and saved before it closes.

Capture a whole web page, chat or long list as one tall picture. A9 Snap scrolls it for you and stitches what it sees. It is a Pro feature. A long page doesn't fit on one screen. Scrolling capture scrolls the area you choose by itself, takes a picture after each scroll, and joins the pictures into one tall PNG that goes through the usual path: onto the clipboard, into your screenshots folder with the next number, into the strip , with the toast and its Edit button. It is part of A9 Snap Pro: see Pro features .

Take one Press Alt + Z . Press L (for long ). The size says Scroll , for example Scroll · 1280 × 720 . (You can also press L after you start dragging, or just before you let go.) Click a window, or drag a region inside the part that scrolls . Dragging only the scrolling area, without the window's title bar and toolbars, gives the cleanest picture. Scrolling starts the moment you let go. If you changed the capture hotkey, the keys follow it: your hotkey, then L . The picker's hint line says L scroll (Pro) . L is never sticky: the next capture starts as a normal picture. L goes with S ( secure capture ): a secure scrolling capture is a secure picture. It replaces R ( record video ): press one and the other turns off. Without Pro, L does not scroll. The picker says Scrolling capture is part of A9 Snap Pro , the capture is a normal picture, and the Pro sheet opens once after the picker closes.

While it scrolls A small bar sits just outside the area, with a Volt dot, the height of the picture so far, and Stop . A thin Volt outline marks the area. Neither is ever in the picture. A9 Snap turns the mouse wheel over the middle of the area (it moves the pointer there while it works and puts it back afterwards), waits for the page to stop moving, takes a frame, and lines it up with the one before by finding the rows they share. It adapts how far it scrolls to how far your app moves for each notch, so frames overlap by about half. It stops by itself when: the page ends (nothing moves any more), or the picture reaches its height limit (see Settings below), or you stop it: press Stop , Esc , or the capture hotkey again. A9 Snap keeps everything captured so far. Headers and footers that stay put while the page scrolls (a sticky menu bar, a status line) are kept once , at the top and bottom of the picture, not repeated in every frame. A scroll bar at the right edge is ignored when frames are lined up. A page that is shorter than the area gives an ordinary picture, and the toast says nothing scrolled .

h: If it can't line the frames up
t: If it can't line the frames up If two scrolls in a row can't be lined up (the page jumps, the content changes while it scrolls), the bar says Scroll it yourself, then press Stop . Scroll with the mouse or keyboard, a screen at a time or less, and A9 Snap keeps stitching what it sees until you press Stop .

What you get One PNG, the next number in your screenshots folder, such as SNAP-0043.png , on the clipboard as a picture. Also copy as file works as for any capture. A toast that says Copied · SNAP-0043.png , with Edit . If the height limit cut the picture, it says stopped at 20,000 px . The app and window it came from are noted like any picture's, and you can search for them in the strip. A secure scrolling capture goes where a secure capture goes.

Settings Open Saving in the Home window. Tallest scrolling capture. 10,000, 20,000 (the default) or 40,000 pixels. A very tall picture on a wide screen takes a lot of memory and a few seconds to save.

Works best with Scrolling capture works best in web browsers and most lists and documents : anything that scrolls smoothly when you turn the mouse wheel over it. Some apps scroll in ways that can't be stitched : pages that move or animate as they scroll, content that loads or changes on its own, apps that ignore the mouse wheel, and views that redraw differently at every position. You get the manual fallback or a partial picture there. It captures the picture a screen at a time, so it can only capture what the app can scroll to. It does not scroll sideways, and PDF viewers are not supported.

Privacy Scrolling capture happens on your PC and the pictures stay there. It only looks at the area you chose and puts the finished picture where any capture goes. Nothing is uploaded and the log says only how many frames there were and how big the picture is. See Privacy .

Send a capture to the app you work in with one click, through Windows' own Share sheet. A9 Snap needs no account, no connection and makes no network call for it. It is a Pro feature. After a capture you usually paste it into a chat, an email or a ticket. Share opens the Windows Share sheet on the capture, so any app that accepts shares is one click away: mail, chat, team apps, nearby sharing and whatever else you have installed. It is part of A9 Snap Pro: see Pro features .

Where to find Share On the confirmation. After a capture, the note at the bottom right has Share next to Edit . A recording's note has it next to Save as GIF and Show in folder . In the strip. Pick a capture (or several) and press H , or right-click one and choose Share… . A recording and a GIF have it too. In the editor. Click Share in the top bar. If you changed the picture, A9 Snap saves it over the capture, the same way Done does, and then opens the Share sheet on the saved file; if you changed nothing, the capture goes as it is and nothing is written. The editor stays open. Without Pro these buttons carry a small PRO badge, and clicking one opens the Pro sheet instead. A secure capture has no Share button anywhere.

What the apps get A picture goes as a file and, for apps that take pictures, as the picture itself. A recording ( .mp4 ) or a GIF goes as a file. Pick several captures in the strip and press H , and they go together as files. Windows decides what the sheet lists. It already puts the apps you used last at the top, and Email is among the targets, so A9 Snap keeps no list of its own.

Privacy A9 Snap hands the file to Windows and does nothing else: no account, no connection, no link, no upload, and no network call of its own. When you pick an app in the sheet, that app takes the file and does what it does; A9 Snap never sees where it went. Free never uses Share, and the log says only that the sheet opened for a number of files, never their names. See Privacy .

If the sheet doesn't open Windows opens the sheet on the screen your pointer is on. If you see Couldn't share , the file may have been moved or deleted since the capture; take it again or find it in the strip . The sheet is part of Windows 10 and 11, so there is nothing to install.
See also The strip Mark up a screenshot Pro features

Double-click any picture or video and A9 Snap shows it at once, in a window the size of the picture, with the rest of the folder one wheel-click away. Zoom with a small map of where you are, turn a picture, play a video, save a frame of it or cut its start and end off (Pro), see the folder as thumbnails, read its info, rename it, then mark it up in the same window, make it ready to send (smaller, another type, no location), copy it or send it. It is free, it writes nothing about what you look at, and it never makes itself your default app. A9 View is the part of A9 Snap that looks at pictures and plays videos. It is for files that did not come from A9 Snap too: a photo from your phone, a download, a logo, a diagram, a screen recording. It opens quickly, shows the picture at its own size, and puts the same tools you use on captures one key away. It is part of the free app, and it lives inside it: one install, one icon in the tray. Videos are described in Videos below.

Open a picture First choose A9 Snap in Windows (see Choose A9 Snap in Windows below), then double-click a picture or a video in Explorer. You can also right-click one and choose Open with , then A9 Snap , without choosing anything first. If A9 Snap is already running, it shows the picture in the A9 View window at once. If it is not, it starts, shows the picture first and then finishes starting up, and stays in the tray as after any start. Select several pictures and press Enter : A9 View shows the first one. Inside A9 View, press Ctrl + O (or the Open button) for a file dialog, or drop a picture, a video or a folder on the window . A folder opens at its first item. One window is used for everything. Opening another picture replaces the one on screen. Closing the window hides it; it is kept ready for the next one. A9 Snap opens PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, BMP, ICO, SVG, TIFF and HEIC pictures. An animated GIF or WebP plays. An SVG is shown as a picture only: nothing in it runs. A photo's stored rotation is respected, so a phone picture is upright. TIFF and HEIC are read by Windows itself; if your PC has no decoder for a type, the window says which type it cannot open and what Windows needs (for HEIC, the free HEIF Image Extensions from the Microsoft Store), and the wheel still moves to the next picture. A picture that cannot be read (damaged, locked or gone) shows its name and the reason in the window.

Size and place By default the window fits the picture. A picture smaller than your screen opens at 100%, never scaled up: one picture pixel is one screen pixel, so it is sharp at any display scale. A bigger one is scaled down to fit inside 90% of the screen's usable area. The window opens in the middle of the monitor your pointer is on, and never smaller than its title bar needs. Change this with A9 View window in Settings : Fit each picture (the default) or Keep my size and place , where the window stays where and how big you left it and each picture fits inside it.

Moving and zooming Do this What happens Mouse wheel The next or previous picture in the same folder. Ctrl +wheel Zooms in and out around the pointer. + / - Zooms in and out around the middle of the window. Left / Right , PgUp / PgDn Previous and next picture (or video). Home / End The first and the last picture. Ctrl + 0 Fits the picture to the window. Ctrl + 1 Shows it at 100%. Drag Moves a zoomed picture around. Double-click or F11 Full screen on and off. Esc Leaves full screen, then closes the window. Delete Sends the file to the Recycle Bin. A note offers Undo (also Ctrl + Z ). It is never deleted for good. Ctrl + C Copies the picture and the file, as a capture is copied. E Edits the picture. See below. P Opens and closes Ready to send . F1 Opens this page. Mouse wheel in A9 View in Settings swaps the wheel and Ctrl +wheel, if you would rather zoom with the wheel alone. The title bar shows the file name, where it is in the folder ("12 of 48"), its size in pixels and on disk, and the zoom. Nothing else is on screen until you move the pointer: then the toolbar and arrows appear.

The mini-map When the picture is bigger than the window shows, a small overview of the whole picture appears at the bottom right, with a rectangle for the part you are looking at. Click or drag in it to move around. The cross closes it until your next zoom, and it hides by itself when the whole picture is in view. It never covers the toolbar. Mini-map in Settings turns it off for good.

The toolbar Move the pointer over the window and a bar appears at the bottom, then fades after a moment. It holds Open , Zoom out , Zoom in , Fit or 100% , Previous , Next , Rotate left , Rotate right , Flip , Edit , Ready to send , Stay on top , Info , Thumbnails and A9 View settings (which opens Settings on this section). Every button's tooltip names its key. Right-click Previous or Next to jump to the first or last picture, or back or forward 10. Toolbar in Settings keeps the bar always shown, or never shown.

Videos A9 View plays MP4, M4V, MOV and WebM videos in the same window, with the same wheel, arrows, zoom, full screen, thumbnails, info, rename and Delete. An animated GIF stays a picture. Nothing here changes or overwrites a video file; Trim (Pro) writes a new one. Opening. Double-click a video in Explorer (once you have chosen A9 Snap for that type), drop one on the window, press Ctrl + O , or start A9 Snap with its path. A video opened this way plays at once . A video you arrive at by moving through the folder shows its first frame and a play button and waits, unless Play videos as I move through a folder is on in Settings. A9 Snap's own recordings open here too: from the Home window, the strip and the note after a recording. Open my recordings in A9 View in Settings (on by default) switches it; off, they open in the app Windows uses for them. The window opens at the video's own pixel size under the same rule as pictures ( Fit each picture or Keep my size and place ). Ctrl +wheel zoom, dragging and the mini-map work on a video as on a picture. Rotate and flip do nothing on a video. A video is read from disk as it plays , a piece at a time, never loaded whole: a two-hour or multi-gigabyte recording opens as fast as a short one.

Controls A row of controls sits just above the toolbar and shows and hides with it: play and pause , a scrub bar with the time so far and the length (drag it and the picture follows), volume and mute , speed (0.5, 1, 1.5 and 2 times) and loop . Do this What happens Click the video, or Space Plays and pauses. At the end it stops on the last frame, unless loop is on. Shift + Left / Shift + Right Jumps 5 seconds back or forward. , / . Steps one frame back or forward (the video pauses first). M Mutes and unmutes. S Save this frame (below). Left / Right and the wheel Still the previous and next item in the folder, so you are never stuck on a video. The volume and the mute switch are remembered between sessions. The speed is 1 each time A9 Snap starts.

Save this frame S , the camera button on the toolbar, or Save this frame in the right-click menu saves the frame on screen as the next numbered capture in your screenshots folder (named like any capture) and copies it. It is the whole video frame at the video's own pixel size, not a picture of the window. It is free.

What a video shows The title bar adds the video's length ("clip.mp4 · 3 of 9 · 800 × 450 · 0:05 · 1.2 MB · 100%"). In the thumbnail strip a video shows a frame with a small play mark, made in memory like the rest and never saved. The info panel ( I ) adds the length , frame rate , video format and audio format , and whether the video has sound . The right-click menu has Save this frame , Trim (Pro), Copy (the file), Share , Show in folder and Delete ; the text and picture tools are for pictures.

Trim (Pro) Trim cuts the start and the end off a video and saves the part you keep as a new file . It is part of A9 Snap Pro : everyone sees the Trim button (it carries a small PRO badge without Pro), and using it without Pro opens the Pro sheet and writes nothing. Press E on a video, or press Trim on the toolbar or in the right-click menu. Two handles appear on the scrub bar, the part outside them is dimmed, and the whole video is kept to begin with. Drag the handles to the first and last moment you want to keep. A handle can't cross the other one, and the shortest part is half a second. Or play or seek to a moment and press [ to start the kept part there, or ] to end it there. Play plays only the kept part and stops at its end. Press Save trimmed video . A progress bar shows while it writes; Cancel stops it and leaves no file . When it is done, the new file is shown in the window. The new file is the next numbered recording in your screenshots folder (named like any recording, so the strip and Home find it), it keeps the sound , and it starts and ends within a tenth of a second of the points you chose. The original is never changed or replaced. Trim writes the new picture with the same encoder A9 Snap's recorder uses (the PC's hardware encoder when it has one, Microsoft's otherwise), so the new file looks like the old one but is made again, not copied; a long video takes a little while. The picture is read at whatever size the video is (a width that is not a multiple of 16 included); if A9 Snap can't read how a video's picture is stored, Trim says so and writes nothing. Press Esc to leave Trim without saving. Trim works on MP4, M4V and MOV videos holding H.264 picture and AAC sound (or none) , which is what A9 Snap records. For any other file, for example a WebM or an MP4 in another format, the button is greyed out and its tooltip says why in one line.

h: A video A9 View can't play
t: A video A9 View can't play A file with a video ending that is not a video, or a format the built-in player does not know, shows A9 View can't play this video with Open with another app , which asks Windows for its Open with list for that file. The wheel and the arrows still move on to the other items. A9 View does not promise to play every format.

Stopping Playback stops, and the file is released, when you move to another item, close the window or A9 View hides. After closing, no sound goes on and you can rename, move or delete the file at once. Delete and F2 work on a video as on a picture.

Rotate and flip R turns the picture a quarter turn to the right and Shift + R to the left. H flips it left to right and V top to bottom. This is only a view : the file is never changed, and the picture goes back to normal when you move to another one. The mini-map, zooming at the pointer and dragging follow the turned picture. To keep the turned picture, right-click and choose Save a copy . It is written as the next numbered capture in your screenshots folder, named like any capture, and copied. The original stays exactly as it was. Dragging the picture out into another app, and Copy , give the file as it is on disk (unless you saved a copy).

Thumbnails G (or the Thumbnails button) shows a row of thumbnails of the folder along the bottom, with the current picture marked. Click one to jump to it; the wheel over the strip scrolls it, and it follows you as you move. Ctrl +click picks or unpicks a thumbnail and Shift +click picks a run of them, for a batch ; a plain click clears the picks. Right-click a thumbnail to show it or to compare it with the picture on screen. The thumbnails are made after the picture is on screen, held in memory only and never saved anywhere. The strip is off to begin with, and A9 View remembers if you turn it on.

Info I opens a panel at the side with the picture's name , folder , type , size on disk , pixel size , and modified and created dates. When the file carries them it also shows the camera , lens , exposure , date taken and location . A value can be copied with the button beside it. The panel only reads; it edits nothing. A location shows as coordinates with Open in maps , which opens a map in your browser. That click is the only way anything about a picture leaves your PC: A9 Snap builds the link from the picture's own coordinates, and sends nothing until you click. See Privacy .
Stay on top T keeps the A9 View window above your other windows until you turn it off or close the window. A pin shows in the title bar while it is on.

Rename F2 renames the picture in its folder. A box opens at the top of the window with the name (without its ending); Enter renames and Esc cancels. The ending stays as it is: renaming never converts a picture. A name that is already taken, or that Windows does not allow, says why and changes nothing. Renaming a capture takes its edit original, its note of where it came from and its searchable text with it, and its number stays taken. Because a capture is found by its numbered name, a capture renamed to something else no longer shows in the strip or on Home.

Order and looping Items come in name order, the way Explorer sorts names : 2 comes before 10 . Right-click the picture, or open Settings , to sort by name , date modified or size , ascending or descending. Loop at the ends (on by default) makes the next item after the last the first, and the other way round; turn it off and the wheel stops at the ends. Pictures and videos are items of the same folder and share one count and one order; Include videos when moving through a folder in Settings leaves the videos out. The next and previous pictures are read ahead, so a step shows at once.
Transparent pictures Transparent pictures in Settings chooses what shows behind the see-through parts of a picture: a checkerboard (the default) or the dark ground of the window.

The right-click menu Right-click the picture for Edit (in this window), Ready to send , Compare with… (Pro), Copy , Copy text , Redact , Share , Show in folder and Delete , then Save a copy while the picture is turned, and the folder's order and Loop at the ends . On a video the menu is Save this frame , Trim (Pro), Copy , Share , Show in folder and Delete , then the same order and Loop at the ends . Copy text , Redact and Share are part of A9 Snap Pro : without it they carry a small PRO badge and open the Pro sheet. Redact copies the picture with its email addresses, phone numbers and card numbers blurred; the file is not changed. See Auto-redact . You can also drag the picture out of the window and drop the file into another app, as in the strip . While you are zoomed in, a drag moves the picture instead; hold Alt to carry the file out.

Edit a picture Press E on a picture (or click Edit on the toolbar, or choose it in the right-click menu) and the editor's tools come up in the same window , on the picture as it is shown: arrow, box, ellipse, highlight, text, numbered steps, stamps, blur, crop, Redact (Pro), Shadow and Copy text , with the same keys and the same look. Your place in the folder, and the thumbnail strip if it is on, stay where they were. A window fitted to a small picture grows to make room for the tools. If the picture is turned or flipped when you press E , editing starts from it as shown and a save writes it as shown. A video is not edited: E on a video is Trim . Press Esc or E again to leave. Because E leaves, the Ellipse tool is O here (in the editor window it is still E ). The wheel and Left and Right still move to the other pictures, and Ctrl +wheel zooms, Space and drag (or the middle button) moves around, and the mini-map follows. Ctrl + Z , Ctrl + Y and Ctrl + Shift + Z undo and redo for the picture you are editing, and Ctrl + C copies the picture with your edits. The Drag file handle drags the file as it is on disk: your edits are in it only after you save.

What saving does A capture (a numbered file A9 Snap took, in your screenshots folder): Ctrl + S or Save saves over it, keeps the untouched original in the hidden .a9snap folder, copies the result, and Revert puts the original back, exactly as in the editor window. Any other picture is never changed. Ctrl + S is Save a copy : it writes name (edited).jpg next to the picture, then name (edited 2).jpg and so on, and never overwrites anything. The copy is in the same format when A9 Snap can write it ( PNG , JPG at high quality, WebP , BMP ). HEIC, SVG, GIF, TIFF, AVIF and ICO are saved as a PNG (a GIF keeps only its first frame), and a line above the picture says so before you save. An animated WebP or PNG also keeps only its first frame, and says so. A copy carries no camera or location data . Save as new capture ( Ctrl + Shift + S ) is there for every picture: it writes the edited picture as the next numbered capture in your screenshots folder and leaves the first picture alone. If the folder can't be written to (a read-only folder, a drive you can't change), A9 View says so, writes nothing, keeps your edits and offers Save as new capture instead . After a save the window shows the file that was saved.

Unsaved edits are asked about Moving to another picture ( Left , Right , the wheel, a thumbnail), closing the window, Ctrl + O , dropping a file on the window or opening another picture from Explorer asks Save , Don't save or Cancel . Save uses the save that fits the picture (over a capture, a copy beside anything else); Cancel keeps every edit and stays where you are. E edits in A9 View in Settings (on by default) switches this. Off, E opens the editor window instead, on a copy for a picture that is not a capture, as in 0.16. The editor window itself, which opens after a capture, from Home and from the strip, is unchanged.

Ready to send A picture that is about to leave your PC often needs one more step: it is too big for an email or a ticket, a form wants another type, or a phone photo carries where it was taken. Press P (or Ready to send on the toolbar or in the right-click menu) and a panel opens beside the picture. Everything happens on your PC, the original is never changed , and it is free. The panel shows the original's size in pixels and on disk, and under it the result's , worked out as you choose (for a very large WebP it shows about how big at once, and the exact size a moment later): Size. Long edge (3840, 2560, 1920 , 1280, 800, or a number you type), Percent (75, 50, 25, or a number), or Original . The shape is kept. A ready-made size never makes a picture bigger; a number you type can. A result is at most 16,384 pixels a side. Type. Keep as is , PNG , JPG or WebP . JPG and WebP have a Quality slider (85 to begin with). Keep as is keeps a PNG, JPG or WebP; a GIF, BMP, TIFF, HEIC, AVIF or ICO becomes a PNG , and a line says so. See-through areas become white in a JPG, with a note. An animated picture gives its first frame only. An SVG can't be made ready. Make it smaller. Under 1 MB , Under 500 KB , Under 200 KB , or Off . A9 View lowers the quality first (never below 40) and makes the picture smaller only if it has to, then says what it chose. If it can't get under the limit, it says that, with the smallest it could make. 1 MB here is 1,000,000 bytes. Remove location and camera details (on to begin with). The line under it lists what the file carries: location , camera , lens , date taken and other tags (such as software, owner, comments and notes), or None found . A photo's stored rotation is applied to the pixels first, so nothing turns sideways. The colour profile stays, because without it the colours would change. Turn this off to keep the camera's own details; the line says which can't be carried over.

Where the result goes Save beside the original writes name (ready).jpg next to the picture, then name (ready 2).jpg and so on. Nothing is ever overwritten. The window then shows the new file. Save as new capture writes the next numbered capture in your screenshots folder. A capture is always a PNG , so with Make it smaller on, the picture is made smaller until the PNG fits. Copy puts the result on the clipboard. If the folder can't be written to , A9 View says so, writes nothing and offers Save as new capture . The choices you last saved with are remembered. Esc or P closes the panel. JPG files are written with code based in part on the work of the Independent JPEG Group.

Batch and side by side (Pro) Doing one picture at a time is free. Many at once and two side by side are part of A9 Snap Pro : everyone sees them with a PRO badge, and using one without Pro opens the Pro sheet and writes nothing.

Many pictures at once Open the panel ( P ) and choose the size, type and the rest as for one picture. Under Make many ready , choose the pictures you picked in the thumbnail strip ( Ctrl +click, Shift +click) or All pictures in this folder . Press Make N pictures ready . A progress bar shows how far it is. You can keep looking around while it works. The results go in a ready folder inside the folder you are looking at. Each keeps its name, with the new ending; a name that is already there gets (2) , and nothing is overwritten. Cancel keeps the files already finished and leaves no half-written one. At the end a summary says how many were made, their total size before and after, and what was skipped and why: videos (never changed), pictures that couldn't be read , and, with Keep as is , types A9 Snap can't write (GIF, BMP, TIFF, HEIC, AVIF, ICO and SVG). Choose PNG, JPG or WebP to include all of them but SVG. Show the ready folder opens it.

Side by side Right-click the picture and choose Compare with… , or right-click a thumbnail and choose Compare with this picture . The picture on screen is shown next to the other one (the next in the folder to begin with, or the other of two picked thumbnails). Zoom and place move together : the wheel zooms both, a drag moves both, Ctrl + 0 fits them and Ctrl + 1 shows the first at 100%. Click a thumbnail, or press Left or Right , to change the other picture. Swap sides changes which is on the left. Save side by side writes one picture holding both, as the next numbered capture in your screenshots folder: a small gap between them, on the window's dark ground (behind a see-through picture, what Transparent pictures is set to), with a label over each ( Before and After to begin with; type your own, or untick Labels ). A pair too big for one picture is scaled down together. The window then shows the saved picture, and Ready to send works on it like any other. Esc closes the comparison.

Choose A9 Snap in Windows Windows lets only you decide which app opens your pictures and videos, so A9 Snap never makes itself the default. What it does is tell Windows that it can open these types, so it appears under Open with and in Windows' Default apps list. Installing A9 Snap changes nothing about what opens your pictures or videos today, and uninstalling removes what it added. In Settings , the A9 View section has Choose A9 Snap in Windows . It opens Windows' Default apps page for A9 Snap, where you pick the types you want it to open, and it lists the types that open with A9 Snap now: the picture types on one line and the video types on their own line , so nobody gets video by surprise. On the Microsoft Store version A9 Snap offers the same types through its package.

Privacy A9 View reads the picture or video and the names of the other files in its folder, and writes nothing: no thumbnails on disk, no frames, no list of what you viewed, no index. The only files it can write are ones you ask for ( Save a copy , Save this frame , Save trimmed video , saving an edit, Ready to send , the ready folder of a batch, or Save side by side ). Ready to send and side by side work on your PC: nothing is uploaded, and no list of the pictures you made ready is kept. Editing a picture that is not a capture writes only the copy you save: no kept original, no thumbnail, no edit mark and no search text; the copy has no camera or location data. A video is read through A9 Snap's own local route, a piece at a time, and no network is involved; nothing is held open between pieces, so the file is free the moment it stops playing. The log says the type, the sizes and the times, never a file or folder name. Secure captures and the secure vault are never opened by A9 View. It makes no network call; the one thing that leaves your PC is the map link you open yourself from the info panel.
